scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__find
tools.description: Search the current page in the Browser pane for elements whose accessibility-tree line (role / name / text) contains `query`, case-insensitively. Returns up to 20 `ref_N` matches usable with `computer`/`form_input`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

query.description: Text to look for in an element's role, name or text (case-insensitive substring, e.g. "Sign in", "search", "Add to cart").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__form_input
tools.description: Set the value of a form element identified by `ref` (from read_page/find). Handles input/textarea/select/checkbox/contenteditable.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__get_page_text
tools.description: Extract the visible text of the Browser pane's page (article/main content first, falls back to body innerText).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__javascript_tool
tools.description: Execute JavaScript in the Browser pane's page for DEBUGGING and INSPECTION only. Do NOT use this to implement UI changes — edit source code instead.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description: Action to perform (only `javascript_exec` is supported).

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. Return values are serialized as JSON.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__navigate
tools.description: Navigate the Browser pane to a URL, or go "back"/"forward" in history. If the Browser pane isn't open yet, this opens it at the URL (no dev server needed).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

force.description: If the page shows a "Leave site?" dialog because of unsaved changes, discard those changes and navigate anyway. Defaults to false.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_list
tools.description: List servers started with preview_start. Returns serverIds for use with other preview_* tools.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_logs
tools.description: Get server stdout/stderr output. Use to check for build errors, verify server behavior, or read debug output. Use 'level' to filter to errors only, or 'search' to filter for specific text. Use after preview_start.

level.description: Filter by level: 'all' (default) shows all output, 'error' shows only lines containing error/exception/failed/fatal

search.description: Filter to lines containing this text (e.g., '[DEBUG]', 'POST /api')

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_start

name.description: Server name from .claude/launch.json.

url.description: URL to open in the Browser pane without a dev server (instead of starting one by `name`).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_stop
tools.description: Stop a server started with preview_start.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_console_messages
tools.description: Get console output (log, info, warn, error, debug) from the Browser pane.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Call again later if you need a different module. Do NOT mention or narrate this call to the user — it is an internal setup step. Call it silently and proceed directly to the visualization in your response.

platform.description: The client platform the widget will render on. Pass 'mobile' when your system prompt indicates a mobile client (narrow ~380px viewport) so SVG viewBox and layout guidance are sized accordingly; otherwise pass 'desktop'. Defaults to 'unknown' (desktop sizing).

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

def parent_key(root):
    """Identity of the code before the change: the commit, plus any uncommitted change outside .py files,
    which the before side shares with the after side. None outside a git repository."""
    try:
        head = _git(root, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD').strip()
        other = [line for line in _git(root, 'status', '--porcelain').splitlines() if not line.rstrip().endswith(('.py', '.pyi'))]
    except OSError:
        return None
    return hashlib.sha256('\n'.join([head, *sorted(other)]).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]


def load_memo(memo, key):
    """The memo for the code before the change ``key``. Outcomes before the change hold only for the same key; the
    measured rates, per-test durations and when each test last flipped carry over to any key. ``rate`` is the median of
    the last measured rates."""
    try:
        data = json.loads(Path(memo).read_text())
    except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
        return dict(key=key, before={}, rate=None, rates=[], durations={}, flips={})
    # A memo written before rates were kept holds one rate.
    rates = data.get('rates') if isinstance(data.get('rates'), list) and data.get('rates') else [data.get('rate')]
    rates = [rate for rate in rates if isinstance(rate, (int, float)) and rate > 0][-RATES:]
    kept = dict(rate=_median(rates), rates=rates, durations=data.get('durations') or {}, flips=data.get('flips') or {})
    return dict(data, **kept) if data.get('key') == key else dict(key=key, before={}, **kept)


def _median(rates):
    return round(statistics.median(rates), 2) if rates else None


def history(memo):
    """({id: when it last flipped}, {id: seconds}) from earlier runs in this tree; empty when there were none."""
    try:
        data = json.loads(Path(memo).read_text())
    except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
        return {}, {}
    return data.get('flips') or {}, data.get('durations') or {}


def execute(runner, python, tree, ids, scratch, name, timeout, parts):
    """runners.execute over ``parts`` processes side by side. Returns ({id: state}, [problems])."""
    slices = [ids[i::parts] for i in range(parts)] if parts > 1 else [ids]
    slices = [part for part in slices if part]
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(len(slices)) as pool:
        results = list(pool.map(lambda pair: runners.execute(runner, python, tree, pair[1], Path(scratch)/f'{name}-{pair[0]}.xml', timeout),
                                enumerate(slices)))
    found, problems = {}, []
    for got, problem in results:
        found.update(got)
        if problem and problem not in problems:
            problems.append(problem)
    return found, problems


def within(seconds, deadline):
    """``seconds``, cut to what is left before ``deadline`` (a time.monotonic() value); unchanged without one."""
    return seconds if deadline is None else min(seconds, deadline - time.monotonic())


def late(deadline):
    """Whether ``deadline`` (a time.monotonic() value) has passed."""
    return deadline is not None and time.monotonic() >= deadline


def run(root, edits, ids, python=None, budget=60, runner=None, memo=None, own=(), base_cache=None, functions=(), generate_with=None,
        merge_base=None, deadline=None, extras=(), prefer=()):
    """Outcomes of ``ids`` before and after the change. Returns (rows, info, gaps). ``prefer``: tests seen running a
    changed line, run first by side-by-side.

    ``own`` are the tests the change adds or edits (replay.touched); they are also run on the code before the change
    with the tests as the change leaves them, and their verdicts go to ``info['replayed']``.

    ``functions`` are the changed functions (analyze's changed_functions): with Python 3.12 or later, the tests that ran
    run once more on the code before the change while each changed function is executed side by side on the inputs
    they call it with (sidebyside); stable differences go to ``info['behaviour']``.

    ``generate_with`` (dollars, minutes, model[, cli]): changed functions the tests never called get model-written probes, kept
    only on execution evidence (generate); results go to ``info['generated']``.

    ``base_cache`` (basecache.BaseCache) answers passing outcomes on the code before the change from earlier runs;
    only what it cannot answer runs there.

    ``memo`` is a file kept between runs on the same tree: outcomes already seen on the code before the change
    (valid while that code is the same) and the measured test rates, whose median plans how many candidates are tried
    first. Time the plan leaves over goes to the next candidates.

    ``merge_base`` is the commit before the change when the tree is its head (a pull request): a file the patch cannot
    be undone in is taken as that commit holds it. A file neither the patch nor the merge base gives stays as the tree
    holds it on both sides, and a gap names it; the rest of the change is still compared.

    ``deadline`` (a time.monotonic() value: CI's wall cap, less time to report) cuts every run at it, and no step starts
    past it. The steps run in order of what they find: flips, the change's own tests, then isolation, side-by-side and
    generated probes. What the deadline left undone or cut short goes to ``info['cut']``."""
    python, gaps, started, cut = python or sys.executable, [], time.perf_counter(), []
    runner = runners.get(root, runner)
    if not ids:
        return [], dict(ran=0, seconds=0.0, runner=runner.name), gaps
    if late(deadline):
        # Not even the copy of the tree: on a large project it takes seconds the report needs.
        cut.append(f'{len(ids)} of {len(ids)} candidate tests')
        return [], dict(ran=0, seconds=0.0, runner=runner.name, candidates=len(ids), cut=cut), gaps
    parts = PARTS if runner.parallel else 1
    seeded, order = trust.ordering(runner, python)
    runner.extra = (*runners.plugin_args(runner, python), *seeded)
    key = parent_key(root) if memo else None
    remembered = load_memo(memo, key) if key else dict(before={}, rate=None, rates=[], durations={}, flips={})
    rate = remembered.get('rate') or RATE
    pool, ids = ids, ids[:max(CHUNK, int(rate * parts * budget * FILL))]
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='amu-shadow-') as scratch:
        if MIRROR is not None:
            other = Path(MIRROR)
            if _mirror_state['synced'] and MIRROR_CHANGED is not None:
                # Only what changed since, and what the last run wrote into the copy, needs copying again.
                _refresh(root, other, set(MIRROR_CHANGED) | _mirror_state['written'] | set(edits))
            else:
                _sync(root, other)
            _mirror_state.update(synced=True, written=set(edits))
        else:
            other = Path(scratch)/'tree'
            shutil.copytree(root, other, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(*IGNORED), symlinks=True)
        on_disk, before_src, after_src, unbuilt = {}, {}, {}, []
        for path, edit in edits.items():
            on_disk[path] = applied(root, path, edit)
            # With the merge base the tree is the change's head: a file not taken for the head was misjudged, and the
            # patch is not applied forward onto it.
            source = original(root, path, edit) if on_disk[path] else None if merge_base else candidate(root, path, edit)
            if source is None and merge_base:
                # The tree is the change's head: the file before the change is the one the merge base holds.
                source, on_disk[path] = file_at(root, merge_base, path), True
            if source is None:
                unbuilt.append(path)
                del on_disk[path]
                continue
            (other/path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            (other/path).write_text(source)
            live = _read(root/path)
            before_src[path], after_src[path] = (source, live) if on_disk[path] else (live, source)
        if unbuilt:
            # The copy keeps such a file as the tree holds it, so both sides run the same file: its change is left out
            # of the comparison, and the rest of the change is not.
            gaps += [f'{path}: other side of the change could not be built; both sides run it as the tree holds it, so its '
                     'change is not compared' for path in unbuilt]
            edits = {path: edit for path, edit in edits.items() if path not in unbuilt}
            key = None  # the copy is not the code before the change: what runs on it is not remembered for that code
            functions = [row for row in functions if row['file'] not in unbuilt]
            if not edits:
                return [], dict(ran=0, seconds=0.0, runner=runner.name), [*gaps, 'no changed file could be built on both sides; nothing executed']
        # Whichever side the working tree holds, the copy holds the other one.
        live_is_after = any(on_disk.values())
        trees = dict(after=root if live_is_after else other, before=other if live_is_after else root)
        states = dict(after={}, before={})
        ready = round(time.perf_counter() - started, 2)  # the copy is made: what comes next runs tests
        context, from_memo = {}, set()
        # Most promising candidates first, in chunks. Each chunk runs on the changed code; only the tests
        # that fail there are run on the code as it was, to confirm they passed before. A test that passes
        # after the change cannot be a new failure, so the unchanged side is never paid for it.
        left, done, aborted, measured, measured_seconds, pace = float(budget), 0, None, 0, 0.0, rate
        first_flip = None  # seconds into the run when the first flip was confirmed (time to first difference)
        stopped, struck = None, {}
        while left > 1:
            if done == len(ids):
                # The planned candidates finished with time to spare: the next ones run a chunk at a time, as many as the
                # last chunk's pace fits in what is left above the share kept for the checks after them. Candidates come
                # shortest first (select.order), so the pace of the whole run would fit too many.
                rate = measured / measured_seconds / parts if measured and measured_seconds else rate
                ids = pool[:done + min(CHUNK * parts, max(0, int(pace * parts * (left - budget * (1 - FILL)))))]
                if done == len(ids):
                    break
            start = done
            chunk = ids[start:start + CHUNK * parts]
            if late(deadline):
                break
            began = time.perf_counter()
            found, problems = execute(runner, python, trees['after'], chunk, scratch, 'after', within(max(left, 1), deadline), parts)
            took = time.perf_counter() - began
            left -= took
            states['after'].update(found)
            for part in _slices(chunk, parts):
                context.update({ident: part for ident in part})
            problem = next((p for p in problems if p != 'timed out'), problems[0] if problems else None)
            # A chunk the runner aborts on does not end the run: the next chunk holds other candidates.
            if problem and problem != 'timed out':
                # Candidates the change removed (a test renamed or deleted in an edited file) cannot run after it; that
                # is not the runner aborting. Only candidates that may still exist on the changed side count. Labels of
                # a group the runner refuses as a whole (runners.refusal) are not lost either: they have their own gap.
                present = [i for i in chunk if not _removed(i, edits, before_src, trees['after'])]
                refused = runners.refusals(runner, trees['after'])
                lost = [i for i in present if found.get(i) in (None, 'unrunnable') and runner.group(i) not in refused]
                if lost:
                    for text in problems:
                        gap = f'shadow run (after the change, {runner.name}): {text}'
                        if text != 'timed out' and text.removeprefix('no outcomes read: ') not in refused.values() and gap not in gaps:
                            gaps.append(gap)
                if present and not any(state != 'unrunnable' for state in states['after'].values()):
                    if lost and problem in struck:
                        # Nothing has run on either side, and another chunk fails as the first did: the runner runs
                        # nothing here, whatever the candidates. Restarting it for every chunk would only use the budget.
                        stopped = (f'shadow run stopped after {start + len(chunk)} of {len(ids)} candidates: {runner.name} ran none of them, '
                                   f'nor the first {struck[problem]} on the code before the change ({problem})')
                        break
                    # Nothing ran on the changed code. If the same candidates run on the code before the change,
                    # the change is what stops the runner: that is a failure of the change, not a gap.
                    began = time.perf_counter()
                    probe, again = runners.execute(runner, python, trees['before'], present, Path(scratch)/'probe.xml',
                                                   within(max(left, CONFIRM), deadline))
                    left -= time.perf_counter() - began
                    ran_before = sum(state != 'unrunnable' for state in probe.values())
                    if ran_before:
                        aborted = dict(error=problem.removeprefix('no outcomes read: '), ran_before=ran_before, probed=len(present))
                        break
                    if lost:
                        struck[problem] = len(present)
            if 'timed out' in problems:
                # A slice cut short ends the run, whatever another slice of the chunk met.
                break
            # The rate counts only chunks that finished: a chunk stopped at the budget took its time and left few
            # outcomes or none.
            if 'timed out' not in problems:
                counted = sum(found.get(ident) in OUTCOMES for ident in chunk)
                measured, measured_seconds = measured + counted, measured_seconds + took
                pace = counted / took / parts if counted and took > 0 else pace
            failing = [ident for ident in chunk if found.get(ident) == 'failed']
            # The code before the change is the same on every run until the commit moves: what it did then, it does now.
            remembered_now = {ident: remembered['before'][ident] for ident in failing if ident in remembered['before']}
            states['before'].update(remembered_now)
            from_memo.update(remembered_now)
            unknown = [ident for ident in failing if ident not in remembered['before']]
            if unknown:
                began = time.perf_counter()
                confirmed, problem = _base(base_cache, runner, python, trees['before'], unknown, Path(scratch)/'before.xml',
                                           within(max(left, CONFIRM), deadline))
                left -= time.perf_counter() - began
                states['before'].update(confirmed)
                remembered['before'].update({ident: state for ident, state in confirmed.items() if state != 'unrunnable'})
                if problem:
                    gaps.append(f'shadow run (before the change, {runner.name}): {problem}')
                if late(deadline) and any(ident not in confirmed for ident in unknown):
                    cut.append(f'confirming {sum(ident not in confirmed for ident in unknown)} failure(s) on the code before the change')
            if first_flip is None and any(_flip(states['before'].get(i), states['after'].get(i)) for i in failing):
                first_flip = round(time.perf_counter() - started, 1)
            done = start + len(chunk)
        if len(ids) < len(pool):
            gaps.insert(0, f'{len(pool) - len(ids)} lower-ranked candidate(s) not run: about {rate:.0f} tests/s per process fit {len(ids)} in the {budget} s allowed')
        if stopped:
            gaps.append(stopped)
        elif done < len(ids) and not aborted and late(deadline):
            cut.append(f'{len(ids) - done} of {len(ids)} candidate tests')
        elif done < len(ids) and not aborted:
            gaps.append(f'shadow run stopped at its {budget} s budget: {done} of {len(ids)} candidates run')
        # A test that an edited test file no longer defines (renamed or deleted) did not fail because of the change: it
        # is gone. Its original form is checked below like any other edited test.
        removed = [i for i in ids if i in states['after'] and _removed(i, edits, before_src, trees['after'])]
        for ident in removed:
            states['after'][ident] = 'removed'
        unstable, edited_flips, originals, replayed, verdicts, edited_verdicts, trust_seconds = [], [], {}, [], {}, {}, 0.0
        side, behaviour, made, generated, mutation, equivalent = None, [], None, [], None, None
        if not aborted:
            # A flip is believed only after the trust checks (trust module): the reach check and three reruns on the
            # changed code. A "before" outcome taken from the memo is confirmed afresh, so a test that is flaky on the
            # unchanged code is not a flip. Nothing is dropped: every flip leaves with a label.
            flipped = [i for i in ids if _flip(states['before'].get(i), states['after'].get(i)) and states['after'][i] == 'failed']
            if flipped:
                ran = [i for i in ids if states['after'].get(i) in OUTCOMES]
                changed = trust.changed_lines(trees['after'], edits, _after_lines)
                began = time.perf_counter()
                verdicts, more = trust.triad(runner, python, trees['after'], flipped, ran, scratch, max(left, CONFIRM), changed,
                                             before_tree=trees['before'], context=context, deadline=deadline)
                # Verifying a flip is not charged to the budget for finding flips: otherwise the reruns could leave no time
                # for the edited-test check below, and flips it would find would go unreported.
                trust_seconds += time.perf_counter() - began
                gaps += more
                if late(deadline) and any(None in verdict['reruns'].values() for verdict in verdicts.values()):
                    cut.append('reruns of flips')
                remembered_flips = [i for i in flipped if i in from_memo and verdicts[i]['label'] != trust.UNSTABLE]
                if remembered_flips:
                    began = time.perf_counter()
                    fresh, _ = _base(base_cache, runner, python, trees['before'], remembered_flips, Path(scratch)/'before-fresh.xml',
                                     within(max(left, CONFIRM), deadline))
                    left -= time.perf_counter() - began
                    for i in remembered_flips:
                        if fresh.get(i) in OUTCOMES and fresh[i] != states['before'][i]:
                            verdicts[i].update(label=trust.UNSTABLE, why='passed and failed on the code before the change')
                unstable += [i for i in flipped if verdicts[i]['label'] == trust.UNSTABLE]
            # A test file the change edited: its tests as they were are also run against the changed code. A test that
            # passed before and fails in its original form on the changed code, but passes, is skipped or is gone as
            # edited, was dealt with by changing the test, not the code: "test edited, not fixed". Only tests the file
            # defined before the edit can run in their original form.
            edited = {path for path in edits if before_src.get(path) and any(_path(i) == path for i in ids)}
            checked = [i for i in ids if _path(i) in edited and states['after'].get(i) in ('passed', 'skipped', 'unrunnable', 'removed')
                       and _existed(i, before_src, trees['after'])]
            # These are tests the change touches, and every test the change touches runs (select): the check gets at least
            # the confirmation allowance even when the candidates used up the budget.
            if checked and late(deadline):
                cut.append('tests of edited files as they were before the edit')
            elif checked:
                # The copy holds one side of every changed file; overwrite it into "changed code, tests as they were".
                for path in edits:
                    _write(other/path, before_src[path] if path in edited else after_src[path])
                failing = []
                try:
                    began = time.perf_counter()
                    originals, problems = execute(runner, python, other, checked, scratch, 'original',
                                                  within(max(left, CONFIRM), deadline), parts)
                    left -= time.perf_counter() - began
                    if 'timed out' in problems and late(deadline):
                        cut.append('tests of edited files as they were before the edit, cut short')
                    failing = [i for i in checked if originals.get(i) == 'failed']
                    if failing:
                        # The same trust checks as any flip, on the changed code with the tests as they were. Reach
                        # counts production lines only: the edited test files are in their earlier form here.
                        changed = trust.changed_lines(other, {p: e for p, e in edits.items() if p not in edited}, _after_lines)
                        began = time.perf_counter()
                        edited_verdicts, more = trust.triad(runner, python, other, failing, checked, scratch, max(left, CONFIRM), changed,
                                                            deadline=deadline)
                        trust_seconds += time.perf_counter() - began
                        gaps += more
                        if late(deadline) and any(None in verdict['reruns'].values() for verdict in edited_verdicts.values()):
                            cut.append('reruns of flips')
                    for problem in problems:
                        gaps.append(f'shadow run (original tests on the changed code, {runner.name}): {problem}')
                finally:
                    for path in edits:
                        _write(other/path, before_src[path] if live_is_after else after_src[path])
                # The before side is run afresh here, not taken from the memo: these become failures on its word alone.
                known = {}
                unknown = list(failing)
                if unknown:
                    began = time.perf_counter()
                    confirmed, problem = _base(base_cache, runner, python, trees['before'], unknown, Path(scratch)/'before-original.xml',
                                               within(max(left, CONFIRM), deadline))
                    left -= time.perf_counter() - began
                    known.update(confirmed)
                    remembered['before'].update({i: state for i, state in confirmed.items() if state != 'unrunnable'})
                    if problem:
                        gaps.append(f'shadow run (before the change, original tests, {runner.name}): {problem}')
                    if late(deadline) and any(i not in confirmed for i in unknown):
                        cut.append(f'confirming {sum(i not in confirmed for i in unknown)} failure(s) of edited tests as they were '
                                   'on the code before the change')

                unstable += [i for i in edited_flips if edited_verdicts.get(i, {}).get('label') == trust.UNSTABLE]

        if own and not aborted and late(deadline):
            cut.append("the change's own tests on the code before it")
        elif own and not aborted:
            replayed, more, unfinished = _replay(runner, python, trees['after'], other, edits, before_src, after_src, live_is_after,
                                                 own, states['after'], scratch, left, base_cache, deadline)
            gaps += more
            if unfinished:
                cut.append(f"the change's own tests on the code before it, {len(unfinished)} of {len(set(own))} left without a result")
        if not aborted:
            # Which hunk makes each counted flip fail (isolate): delta debugging on a copy of the code before the change.
            counted = [i for i in ids if i in verdicts and trust.counted(verdicts[i]['label'])][:ISOLATED]
            for ident in counted:
                if late(deadline):
                    cut.append('flip isolation')
                    break
                began = time.perf_counter()
                found = isolate.run(runner, python, trees['before'], edits, before_src, ident, scratch,
                                    within(ISOLATE_SECONDS, deadline))
                trust_seconds += time.perf_counter() - began
                if found:
                    verdicts[ident]['isolated'] = found
        if functions and not aborted and _monitoring(python) and late(deadline):
            if any(states['after'].get(i) in OUTCOMES for i in ids if i not in set(own)):
                cut.append('side-by-side')
        elif functions and not aborted and _monitoring(python):
            spec_targets, skipped = sidebyside.targets(functions, before_src, after_src)
            # Not the change's own tests: this run uses the tests as they were, where an added test does not exist and
            # an unknown label makes the runner reject the whole batch.
            mine = set(own)
            ran_ids = [i for i in ids if states['after'].get(i) in OUTCOMES and i not in mine]

"""Side-by-side execution of changed functions on captured inputs (Python 3.12 and later).

While candidate tests run on the code before the change, a sys.monitoring hook watches the changed functions. When one
starts, its arguments are snapshotted with pickle (a deep copy that also bounds size), and the function is executed
right there, in the test's own process and state, twice in its version before the change and twice in its version
after, each time on a fresh copy of the arguments. Compared: the return value (or the exception raised), the arguments
afterwards (mutation), what was printed, and the sequence of calls made from first-party code to code outside it. A
difference is kept only when both versions repeat themselves exactly; one that does not is nondeterministic and dropped.

Both versions are compiled from source the same way (decorators left off, so a wrapper's own behaviour is not compared),
in the module's globals, with ``__class__`` bound for ``super()`` and their own name looked up in those globals, as in the
module (recursion reaches the version swapped in for the run); a decorated module function's own name is the copy itself,
so its recursion is undecorated too. Each is named as the source names it, as is everything defined in it. Then the
test's own call goes on as usual. A function that is nested, a coroutine, a generator on one side only, or a method using
a private name that a class body would mangle is not compared, and is counted as such; so is a function in a test file
(the tests, not the code they test), and one whose code is the same once its docstring is set aside (only the docstring,
comments or layout changed).

This runs the project's code on inputs it was really called with; it is a run of its own on the code before the change,
separate from the comparison of test outcomes, whose results it does not touch.

import copy
import json
import re
import textwrap

CALLS = 5          # calls captured per argument shape of a changed function, per process
SHAPES = 8         # argument shapes sampled per changed function, per process
LISTED = 100       # captured calls named in the report
PRIVATE = re.compile(r'(?<![\w.])__[A-Za-z]\w*(?<!__)\b')

            space = dict(globs)

def amu_command(patch, python, runner, budget, generate=None, merge_base=None, deadline=None, extras=()):
    command = [sys.executable, *SAFE, '-m', 'amu.core', '--repo', '.', '--patch-file', str(patch), '--run', '--full-evidence',
               '--python', python]
    if merge_base:
        # A file the patch cannot be undone in is taken from the merge base, not lost with the whole run.
        command += ['--merge-base', merge_base]
    if generate and (generate[0] > 0 or generate[3:4] == (True,)):
        dollars, minutes, model, *cli = generate
        command += ['--generate-dollars', str(dollars), '--generate-minutes', str(minutes), '--generate-model', model]
        command += ['--generate-cli'] if cli and cli[0] else []
    if runner:
        command += ['--runner', runner]
    if budget:
        command += ['--budget', str(budget)]
    if deadline:
        command += ['--deadline', str(deadline)]
    if extras:
        command += ['--extras', ','.join(extras)]
    return command


def bounded(command, cwd, seconds):
    """Run a command in its own process group; past ``seconds`` the whole group is killed. Returns
    (CompletedProcess, None) or (None, 'timed out')."""
    process = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=cwd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True,
                               stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)
    try:
        stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=max(1, seconds))
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        try:
            os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        except OSError:
            pass
        process.communicate()
        return None, 'timed out'
    return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, process.returncode, stdout, stderr), None


def recording(repo, calls=False):
    return cache_dir(repo)/('edges' if calls else 'observed')


def amu_share(budget):
    """Seconds of the wall cap kept for amu itself before a recording may start: the budget for each side, the
    side-by-side run's cap, and a minute for the index and the rest."""
    return 2 * (budget or 60) + SIDE_BY_SIDE + 60


def remove_hooks(python):
    """Take the recorders' hook files out of the interpreter's site-packages. A recording stopped at its limit is
    killed before it can remove them itself, and every test process the interpreter starts afterwards would load them.
    Returns the sweep's gaps."""
    return sitehooks.sweep(python)


def earlier_attempt(repo, calls):
    try:
        attempt = json.loads((cache_dir(repo)/ATTEMPT).read_text())
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return None
    return attempt if isinstance(attempt, dict) and attempt.get('calls') == calls else None


def observe(repo, found, python, runner, seconds):
    """Record the suite on the merge base, in at most ``seconds``, and keep the recording with the head's index:
    per-test call edges on Python 3.12 and later (the sys.monitoring tracer), coverage contexts below that. A recording
    that does not finish is not kept, and is not tried again with no more time than it had. Returns a note for the
    gaps, or None."""
    calls = core_edges.supported(python)
    if recording(repo, calls).is_dir():
        return None
    earlier = earlier_attempt(repo, calls)
    if earlier and earlier.get('seconds', 0) >= seconds:
        return (f"recording skipped: an earlier one did not finish in {earlier['seconds']} s and this run has {seconds} s "
                f"for it; static ranking only")
    scratch = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='amu-base-'))
    tree = scratch/'tree'
    try:
        if git(repo, 'worktree', 'add', '--detach', '--quiet', str(tree), found) is None:
            return 'recording skipped: the merge base could not be checked out'
        # The suite stops itself first, so the recorder removes its own hook; the kill at ``seconds`` is the backstop.
        command = [sys.executable, *SAFE, '-m', 'amu.core', '--repo', str(tree), '--observe-calls' if calls else '--observe',
                   '--python', python, '--observe-seconds', str(max(1, seconds - RECORDING_STORE))]
        done, problem = bounded(command + (['--runner', runner] if runner else []), tree, seconds)
        try:
            gaps = json.loads(done.stdout).get('gaps', []) if done else []
        except (ValueError, AttributeError):
            gaps = []
        unfinished = problem or any('did not finish' in str(gap) for gap in gaps)
        source = recording(tree, calls)
        if unfinished:
            cache_dir(repo).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            (cache_dir(repo)/ATTEMPT).write_text(json.dumps(dict(calls=calls, seconds=seconds, merge_base=found)))
            return f'recording on the merge base did not finish in its share of {seconds} s; static ranking only'
        if not source.is_dir():
            return 'recording on the merge base produced nothing; static ranking only'
        shutil.copytree(source, recording(repo, calls), dirs_exist_ok=True)
        (cache_dir(repo)/ATTEMPT).unlink(missing_ok=True)
        return None
    finally:
        remove_hooks(python)
        git(repo, 'worktree', 'remove', '--force', str(tree))
        shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)


def updated_apart(report):
    """A test the pull request edited, failing only as it was before the edit, is not a flip: the edit is in the diff.
    It moves from the flips to ``updated_tests``, so the flip count, the fresh-job rerun and the counters leave it out.
    (The engine keeps it among its failures, labelled: an agent editing a test to make it pass is told so.)"""
    failures = report.get('predicted_failures')
    if not isinstance(failures, list):
        return report
    edited = [row for row in failures if isinstance(row, dict) and row.get('label') == EDITED]
    if not edited:
        return report
    kept = [row for row in failures if row not in edited]
    report = dict(report, predicted_failures=kept, updated_tests=[*(report.get('updated_tests') or []), *edited])
    if isinstance(report.get('flips'), int):
        report['flips'] = len(kept)
    return report


def run(repo, base, head, out, python=None, runner=None, pr=None, budget=None, install_ok=None, amu_ref=None,
        wall_cap=None, record=False, counters=False, generate=None, extras=()):
    repo, out = Path(repo).resolve(), Path(out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    meta = dict(pr=pr, base=base, head=head, merge_base=None, amu_version=__version__, amu_ref=amu_ref,
                runner=runner or None, budget=budget, wall_cap=wall_cap, install_ok=install_ok, status=None, seconds=None,
                cached_index=cache_dir(repo).is_dir(), recording=None, counters=bool(counters), deadline=None)
    started = time.monotonic()
    # Before anything: a hook an earlier recording could not remove (killed) would load in every test process.
    report, notes = None, sitehooks.sweep(python or sys.executable)
    deadline = started + wall_cap if wall_cap else None

    def left():
        return None if deadline is None else deadline - time.monotonic() - RESERVE
    try:
        live = git(repo, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD')
        if head and live != head:
            report = dict(error=f'the checkout is at {live}, not the pull request head {head}; nothing was run')
        elif (found := merge_base(repo, base, head or 'HEAD')) is None:
            report = dict(error=f'no merge base between {base} and {head}; fetch the history (fetch-depth: 0)')
        else:
            meta['merge_base'] = found
            diff = git(repo, 'diff', '--no-color', '--no-ext-diff', found, head or 'HEAD')
            patch = out/'patch.diff'
            patch.write_text((diff + '\n') if diff else '')
            if not diff:
                report = dict(error='the pull request changes nothing against its merge base; nothing was run')
            else:
                if record:
                    # The recording has its own share: what the wall cap leaves after amu's.
                    share = None if deadline is None else int(left() - amu_share(budget))
                    if share is not None and share < RECORDING_MIN:
                        notes.append(f'recording skipped: the wall cap leaves {max(share, 0)} s for it after amu\'s share')
                    else:
                        note = observe(repo, found, python or sys.executable, runner, 7200 if share is None else share)
                        notes += [note] if note else []
                meta['recording'] = recording(repo).is_dir() or recording(repo, calls=True).is_dir()
                seconds = left()
                if seconds is not None and seconds < 1:
                    report = dict(error=f'stopped at the wall cap of {wall_cap} s before amu ran')
                else:
                    # amu stops starting steps at its deadline and reports what it found; the kill at the wall cap is the
                    # backstop.
                    meta['deadline'] = None if seconds is None else max(1, int(seconds - min(FINISH, seconds / 4)))
                    done, problem = bounded(amu_command(patch, python or sys.executable, runner, budget, generate, found, meta['deadline'], extras),
                                            repo, seconds if seconds is not None else 24 * 3600)
                    if problem:
                        report = dict(error=f'stopped at the wall cap of {wall_cap} s; amu reported nothing', gaps=[
                            f"amu did not report within {round(seconds - meta['deadline'])} s of its deadline of {meta['deadline']} s "
                            'and was stopped: what it found before the wall cap is lost'] if meta['deadline'] else [])
                    else:
                        try:
                            report = json.loads(done.stdout)
                        except ValueError:
                            tail = (done.stderr or done.stdout or 'no output').strip().splitlines()[-1:] or ['no output']
                            report = dict(error=f'amu exited with status {done.returncode} and no report: {tail[0][:300]}')
    except OSError as exc:
        report = dict(error=f'could not run: {exc}')
    if notes and isinstance(report.get('gaps'), list):
        report['gaps'] = notes + report['gaps']
    report = updated_apart(report)
    meta['seconds'] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 1)
    meta['status'] = 'error' if 'error' in report else 'ran'
    (out/'report.json').write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=1))
    (out/'meta.json').write_text(json.dumps(meta, indent=1))
    outputs = os.environ.get('GITHUB_OUTPUT')
    if outputs:
        with open(outputs, 'a') as handle:
            handle.write(f"merge-base={meta['merge_base'] or ''}\n")
            handle.write(f"flips={'' if report.get('flips') is None else report['flips']}\n")
    return report, meta


def main(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog='amu ci run', description=__doc__.split('\n')[0])
    p.add_argument('--repo', default='.')

"""B2: changed functions executed side by side on the inputs the tests call them with."""
import difflib
import sys

import pytest

from amu.core import analyze

NEW = sys.version_info >= (3, 12)
pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not NEW, reason='sys.monitoring needs Python 3.12')


def change(tmp_path, files_before, files_after):
    for name, text in files_after.items():
        (tmp_path/name).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (tmp_path/name).write_text(text)
    diff = ''.join(''.join(difflib.unified_diff(files_before.get(n, '').splitlines(True), files_after[n].splitlines(True),
                                                'a/' + n if n in files_before else '/dev/null', 'b/' + n))
                   for n in files_after if files_before.get(n) != files_after[n])
    return analyze(tmp_path, diff, full_evidence=True, index_dir=tmp_path/'.index', run=True, python=sys.executable)


def test_a_behaviour_change_no_test_catches_is_reported_with_its_input(tmp_path):
    lib0 = 'def clamp(v, top=10):
    return min(v, top)
'
    lib1 = 'def clamp(v, top=10):
    return min(v, top - 1)
'
    tests = 'from lib import clamp


def test_small():
    assert clamp(3) == 3
'
    report = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': lib0, 'tests/test_lib.py': tests}, {'lib.py': lib1, 'tests/test_lib.py': tests})
    assert report['flips'] == 0, report['summary']
    assert report['side_by_side']['compared_calls'] == 1 and report['side_by_side']['targets'] == 1, report['side_by_side']
    assert report['behaviour_differences'] == [], report['behaviour_differences']  # clamp(3) is 3 either way
    tests2 = tests + '

def test_big():
    assert clamp(50) > 0
'
    report = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': lib0, 'tests/test_lib.py': tests2}, {'lib.py': lib1, 'tests/test_lib.py': tests2})
    [row] = report['behaviour_differences']
    assert row['target'] == 'lib.py#clamp' and row['differs'] == ['result'] and '50' in row['input'], row
    assert row['before']['result'] == ['return', '10'] and row['after']['result'] == ['return', '9'], row
    from amu.ci.render import render
    body = render(report, dict(head='a' * 40, merge_base='b' * 40))
    assert '<summary>Behaviour differs on captured input (1)</summary>' in body and '`lib.py#clamp`' in body, body
    assert body.splitlines()[0].endswith('; 1 behaviour difference on captured input, collapsed at the end'), body


def test_mutation_printing_and_exceptions_count_and_noise_does_not(tmp_path):
    lib0 = ('import random


def add(items, x):
    items.append(x)
    return len(items)


'
            'def shout(x):
    print(x)


def parse(x):
    return int(x)


def noisy(x):
    return random.random() + x
')
    lib1 = ('import random


def add(items, x):
    items.append(x)
    items.append(x)
    return len(items) - 1


'
            'def shout(x):
    print(x.upper())


def parse(x):
    return int(x, 16)


def noisy(x):
    return random.random() + x + 0
')
    tests = ('from lib import add, shout, parse, noisy


def test_all():
    add([], 1)
    shout("hi")
'
             '    parse("10")
    noisy(1)
')
    report = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': lib0, 'tests/test_lib.py': tests}, {'lib.py': lib1, 'tests/test_lib.py': tests})
    found = {row['target'].split('#')[1]: row['differs'] for row in report['behaviour_differences']}
    assert found == {'add': ['args_after'], 'shout': ['stdout'], 'parse': ['result']}, report['behaviour_differences']
    assert report['side_by_side']['unstable'] == 1  # noisy: neither version repeats itself, so nothing is said


def test_a_method_using_super_is_compared_with_its_class(tmp_path):
    lib0 = ('class Base:
    def size(self):
        return 1


class Box(Base):
    def __init__(self, n):
        self.n = n

'
            '    def size(self):
        return super().size() + self.n
')
    lib1 = lib0.replace('return super().size() + self.n', 'return super().size() * self.n')
    tests = 'from lib import Box


def test_box():
    assert Box(2).size()
'
    report = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': lib0, 'tests/test_lib.py': tests}, {'lib.py': lib1, 'tests/test_lib.py': tests})
    [row] = report['behaviour_differences']
    assert row['target'] == 'lib.py#Box.size' and row['before']['result'] == ['return', '3'] and row['after']['result'] == ['return', '2'], row


def test_a_function_reaching_its_own_name_finds_the_module_function(tmp_path):
    # Found on sympy #30715: the copy's own name (to_NNF recursing) was a cell of the wrapper it is compiled in, filled
    # with the class owning it, None for a module function. Callers of the changed to_NNF raised "'NoneType' object is not
    # callable" as changed only, and to_NNF itself raised on both sides. A method named like the module function it calls
    # reached its class.
    lib0 = ('def flatten(items):
    out = []
    for item in items:
        out += flatten(item) if isinstance(item, list) else [item]
'
            '    return out


def size(items):
    return len(flatten(items))


'
            'class Bag:
    def __init__(self, items):
        self.items = items

    def size(self):
        return size(self.items)
')
    lib1 = (lib0.replace('else [item]
', 'else [item] if item is not None else []
')
            .replace('return len(flatten(items))', 'return len(flatten(items if isinstance(items, list) else [items]))')
            .replace('return size(self.items)', 'return size(self.items) * 1'))
    tests = 'from lib import Bag, size


def test_size():
    assert size([1, [2, None]]) >= 2
    assert Bag([1, [2, None]]).size() >= 2
'
    report = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': lib0, 'tests/test_lib.py': tests}, {'lib.py': lib1, 'tests/test_lib.py': tests})
    found = {(row['target'].split('#')[1], row['input']): row for row in report['behaviour_differences']}
    outer = found.get(('flatten', '([[1, [2, None]]], {})'))
    assert outer and outer['before']['result'] == ['return', ['list', ['1', '2', 'None']]], found

"""The execution recorder: watched lines per test and calls into watched functions, from a side's own run."""
import subprocess
import sys
import textwrap

import pytest

from amu.core import record, runners

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(sys.version_info < (3, 12), reason='sys.monitoring needs Python 3.12')

PACKAGE = {
    'src/pkg/__init__.py': 'from ._impl import shape, Box\n',
    'src/pkg/__init__.pyi': 'def shape(value: object) -> str: ...\nclass Box: ...\n',
    'src/pkg/_impl.py': textwrap.dedent('''\
        def shape(value):
            if isinstance(value, list):
                return "list"
            return "other"


        class Box:
            __slots__ = ("size",)

            def __init__(self, size):
                self.size = size

            def grow(self, by):
                self.size += by
                return self.size
        '''),
    'tests/test_shape.py': textwrap.dedent('''\
        from pkg import shape, Box


        def test_list():
            assert shape([1]) == "list"


        def test_other():
            assert shape(3) == "other"


        def test_box():
            assert Box(2).grow(1) == 3


        def test_nothing():
            assert True
        '''),
    'tests/test_unit.py': textwrap.dedent('''\
        import unittest

        from pkg import shape


        class ShapeCase(unittest.TestCase):
            def test_list(self):
                self.assertEqual(shape([]), "list")
        '''),
}


def project(tmp_path):
    for name, text in PACKAGE.items():
        (tmp_path/name).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (tmp_path/name).write_text(text)
    return tmp_path


def run(tmp_path, command, lines, targets, cwd=None):
    env = runners.environment(tmp_path, record.prepare(tmp_path/'.rec', tmp_path, lines, targets))

    project(tmp_path)

    assert record.tests_on(coverage, 'src/pkg/_impl.py', [4]) == {'tests/test_shape.py::test_other'}, coverage
    assert 'tests/test_shape.py::test_nothing' not in coverage
    assert calls == []

    assert by['tests/test_shape.py::test_list', 'src/pkg/_impl.py#shape']['output_shown'] == '["return", "\'list\'"]'
    # The same call made again gives the same digests: they are stable across processes.
    _, again, _ = run(tmp_path, [sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest', '-q', '-p', 'no:cacheprovider', 'tests/test_shape.py'], {}, targets)
    assert {(c['test'], c['function'], c['input'], c['output']) for c in again} == \
        {(c['test'], c['function'], c['input'], c['output']) for c in calls}


def test_an_exception_is_the_output_of_the_call_it_left(tmp_path):

    (tmp_path/'src/pkg/_impl.py').write_text(PACKAGE['src/pkg/_impl.py'].replace('return "other"', 'raise ValueError(value)'))
    (tmp_path/'tests/test_shape.py').write_text(PACKAGE['tests/test_shape.py'].replace(
        'assert shape(3) == "other"', 'import pytest\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        shape(3)'))
    _, calls, _ = run(tmp_path, [sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest', '-q', '-p', 'no:cacheprovider', 'tests/test_shape.py'], {},
                      [('src/pkg/_impl.py', 'shape')])
    [other] = [c for c in calls if c['test'] == 'tests/test_shape.py::test_other']
    assert other['output_shown'].startswith('["raise", "ValueError", "3"]'), other


def test_pairing_compares_only_equal_inputs():
    def call(test, n, i, o):
        return dict(test=test, function='m.py#f', n=n, input=i, output=o, input_shown=i, output_shown=o)
    before = [call('t::a', 0, 'x', '1'), call('t::a', 1, 'y', '2'), call('t::b', 0, 'z', '3')]
    after = [call('t::a', 0, 'x', '9'), call('t::a', 1, 'Y', '2'), call('t::c', 0, 'z', '3')]
    rows, counts = record.pair(before, after)
    assert [(r['test'], r['n'], r['before'], r['after']) for r in rows] == [('t::a', 0, '1', '9')]
    assert counts == dict(paired=2, compared=1, inputs_differ=1, unpaired=2, unreadable=0)

- on the code before the change (``base``): the body of the innermost function holding the hunk there, so any test that
  entered that function counts; for a hunk outside any function, its removed lines and the context lines around it;
- on the code after it (``head``): the lines the hunk adds, or, for a hunk that only removes, the lines around the gap.

A hunk with no function around it on the base side and nothing it removed there (code the change adds, such as a new
function) has no base lines: no run of the code before the change can say which tests reach it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ast


def _functions(text):
    """[(first body line, last line, qualified name)] of every function in ``text``; [] when it does not parse."""
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(text or '')
    except (SyntaxError, ValueError):
        return []
    found = []

    def walk(nodes, prefix):
        for node in nodes:
            if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
                qual = prefix + node.name
                if node.body:
                    found.append((node.body[0].lineno, node.end_lineno, qual))
                walk(node.body, qual + '.<locals>.')
            elif isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
                walk(node.body, prefix + node.name + '.')
            elif hasattr(node, 'body') and isinstance(getattr(node, 'body'), list):
                walk(node.body, prefix)
                walk(getattr(node, 'orelse', []) or [], prefix)
                walk(getattr(node, 'finalbody', []) or [], prefix)
                for handler in getattr(node, 'handlers', []) or []:
                    walk(handler.body, prefix)
    walk(tree.body, '')
    return found


def innermost(functions, lines):
    """The narrowest function whose body holds every line in ``lines``, as (first, last, qual); None if none does."""
    lines = sorted(lines)
    if not lines:
        return None
    holding = [f for f in functions if f[0] <= lines[0] and lines[-1] <= f[1]]
    return min(holding, key=lambda f: f[1] - f[0]) if holding else None


def split(path, edit, before, after):
    """The hunks of one file's change, each a dict: path, index, removed and added line numbers, context lines on each
    side, the function holding it on each side, and the lines to watch on each side (``base``, ``head``)."""
    old_functions, new_functions = _functions(before), _functions(after)
    found = []
    for index, (old_start, body, new_start) in enumerate(edit.get('hunks', [])):
        old_line, new_line = old_start, new_start
        removed, added, old_context, new_context = [], [], [], []
        for row in body:
            sign = row[:1]
            if sign == '-':
                removed.append(old_line)
                old_line += 1
            elif sign == '+':
                added.append(new_line)
                new_line += 1
            else:
                old_context.append(old_line)
                new_context.append(new_line)
                old_line += 1
                new_line += 1
        # Where the hunk sits on each side: what it removes or adds, else the gap between its context lines.
        old_here = removed or [n for n in old_context if n < (old_context[-1] if old_context else 0)][-1:] or old_context[:1]
        new_here = added or [n for n in new_context if n < (new_context[-1] if new_context else 0)][-1:] or new_context[:1]
        old_function = innermost(old_functions, removed or old_here)
        new_function = innermost(new_functions, added or new_here)
        if old_function:
            base = set(range(old_function[0], old_function[1] + 1))
        elif removed:
            base = set(removed) | set(old_context)
        elif new_function is None:
            base = set(old_context)  # module or class level: the lines around the insertion run when it runs
        else:
            base = set()  # inside a function the code before the change does not have
        head = set(added) if added else set(new_context)
        found.append(dict(path=path, index=index, removed=removed, added=added, old_start=old_start, new_start=new_start,
                          old_function=old_function[2] if old_function else None,
                          new_function=new_function[2] if new_function else None,
                          base=sorted(base), head=sorted(head)))
    return found


def name(hunk):
    """``path:line`` where the hunk starts on the code after the change."""
    line = (hunk['added'] or [hunk['new_start']])[0]
    return f"{hunk['path']}:{line}"

Only runs when the caller asks for it. It executes the repository's own tests with the
interpreter the caller names, so it belongs to the developer working on their own tree.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import fnmatch
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import statistics
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

from . import basecache, equivalence, generate, isolate, mutate, replay, runners, sidebyside, trust
from .git import _git, file_at
from .patch import applied, candidate, original, renumber

CHUNK = 40
SIDE_BY_SIDE = 120  # seconds at most for the side-by-side run on the code before the change
EXTRAS_SECONDS = 120  # for each of mutation and equivalence, when turned on (build queue part 4)
ISOLATED = 3  # flips whose hunk is isolated
ISOLATE_SECONDS = 120  # per flip
CONFIRM = 20  # seconds always allowed for confirming a failure on the unchanged code
PARTS = max(1, min(4, (os.cpu_count() or 2) // 2))  # processes side by side, for runners that allow it
RATE = 15.0  # tests per second per process, until a run in this tree has measured it
RATES = 9  # measured rates kept; the estimate is their median, so one slow run does not set it
FILL = 0.8  # share of the budget the candidates are planned to fill; the rest is kept for the checks after them
IGNORED = ('.git', '.amu', '.amu-index', '.venv', 'venv', 'node_modules', '__pycache__', '.tox', '.nox',
           '.mypy_cache', '.pytest_cache', '.ruff_cache', 'dist', 'build', '*.egg-info', '.coverage', 'coverage.json')
# A process that stays (amu watch) sets a folder here: the copy of the tree is kept there between runs and brought up to
# date file by file, instead of being made afresh (2.2 s on Django, more than the rest of a warm run).
MIRROR = None
MIRROR_CHANGED = None  # paths, relative to the tree, that changed since the last run (amu watch's events); None: all
_mirror_state = dict(synced=False, written=set())

import difflib
import json
import sys
import textwrap

import pytest

from amu.core import analyze

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(sys.version_info < (3, 12), reason='sys.monitoring needs Python 3.12')

IMPL = textwrap.dedent('''\
    def shape(value):
        if isinstance(value, list):
            return [shape(v) for v in value]
        return type(value).__name__
    ''')
FILES = {
    # A package that re-exports, beside a stub of the same module: resolving `from pkg import shape` by name finds the
    # stub's declaration, not the code.
    'src/pkg/__init__.py': 'from ._impl import shape as shape\n',
    'src/pkg/__init__.pyi': 'def shape(value: object) -> object: ...\n',
    'src/pkg/_impl.py': IMPL,
    'tests/test_shape.py': textwrap.dedent('''\
        import pkg


        def test_nested():
            assert pkg.shape([1, [2]]) == ["int", ["int"]]


        def test_flat():
            assert pkg.shape(1) == "int"
        '''),
    'tests/test_other.py': 'def test_unrelated():\n    assert 1 + 1 == 2\n',
}


def change(tmp_path, after_impl, **kwargs):
    for name, text in FILES.items():
        (tmp_path/name).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (tmp_path/name).write_text(text)
    (tmp_path/'src/pkg/_impl.py').write_text(after_impl)
    diff = ''.join(difflib.unified_diff(IMPL.splitlines(True), after_impl.splitlines(True), 'a/src/pkg/_impl.py', 'b/src/pkg/_impl.py'))
    return analyze(tmp_path, diff, full_evidence=True, index_dir=tmp_path/'.index', run=True, python=sys.executable, **kwargs)


BROKEN = IMPL.replace('return [shape(v) for v in value]', 'return [shape(v) for v in value][::-1]')


def test_a_suite_that_fits_runs_whole_on_both_sides(tmp_path):
    report = change(tmp_path, BROKEN)
    assert report['selection_evidence']['mode'] == 'all of the suite', report['selection_evidence']
    assert report['executed']['ran'] == 3, report['executed']
    assert [row['id'] for row in report['predicted_failures']] == ['tests/test_shape.py::test_nested'], report['summary']
    [hunk] = report['hunks']
    assert hunk['head_tests'] == ['tests/test_shape.py::test_nested'], hunk  # the test that runs the changed line


def test_past_the_budget_the_candidates_are_the_tests_seen_in_the_changed_function(tmp_path):
    # A first run records the suite; a later one, with the suite known not to fit, chooses from that recording.
    change(tmp_path, BROKEN)
    memo = tmp_path/'.index'/'shadow-memo.json'
    data = json.loads(memo.read_text())
    data['suite_seconds'] = 10_000
    memo.write_text(json.dumps(data))
    report = change(tmp_path, BROKEN)

    assert [row['id'] for row in report['predicted_failures']] == ['tests/test_shape.py::test_nested'], report['summary']


def test_static_selection_alone_misses_them_which_is_why_it_is_not_primary(tmp_path):
    report = change(tmp_path, BROKEN, extras=('static-select',))
    assert 'selection_evidence' not in report
    assert report['predicted_failures'] == [], report['summary']  # the failing test was never a candidate
