def is_test_file(path):
    """The rule amu.core.replay uses: under a tests directory, test_*.py, *_test.py, tests.py or conftest.py."""
    parts = str(path).split('/')
    name = parts[-1]
    return name.endswith('.py') and ('tests' in parts[:-1] or name.startswith('test_') or name.endswith('_test.py')
                                     or name in ('tests.py', 'conftest.py'))


def split_flips(report):
    """(flips, tests the pull request updated): a test the pull request edited, failing only as it was before the edit,
    is not a flip. Reports from before 0.4.0 keep those among the flips, labelled; newer ones list them apart."""
    failures = [row for row in report.get('predicted_failures') or [] if failure_id(row)]
    updated = [row for row in failures if isinstance(row, dict) and row.get('label') == EDITED]
    updated += [row for row in report.get('updated_tests') or [] if isinstance(row, dict) and row.get('id')]
    return [row for row in failures if not (isinstance(row, dict) and row.get('label') == EDITED)], updated


def reach(report):
    """Whether something ran the changed code: True, False (side-by-side watched every comparable changed function
    and no test called one), or None (not seen). With False, the production files those functions are in."""
    counted, updated = split_flips(report)
    side = report.get('side_by_side') if isinstance(report.get('side_by_side'), dict) else None
    if counted or updated or report.get('change_evidence') or (side and side.get('functions_called')):
        return True, []
    if any(isinstance(row, dict) and row.get('expect') == 'ran_changed_lines' for row in report.get('tests') or []):
        return True, []
    files = sorted({row.get('file') for row in report.get('changed_functions') or []
                    if isinstance(row, dict) and isinstance(row.get('file'), str) and not is_test_file(row['file'])})
    if side and side.get('targets') and not side.get('functions_called') and files:
        return False, files
    return None, []


# side-by-side's reason (amu/core/sidebyside.py) for a changed function whose code is the same once docstrings,
# comments and layout are set aside.
DOCS_ONLY = 'only its docstring, comments or layout changed'


def docs_only(report):
    """Every change outside the tests is to docstrings, comments or layout: side-by-side found each changed production
    function differs only there, and nothing else in those files changed (no data, class or module-level line)."""
    side = report.get('side_by_side') if isinstance(report.get('side_by_side'), dict) else {}
    reasons = side.get('not_compared') if isinstance(side.get('not_compared'), dict) else {}
    functions = {f"{row['file']}#{row.get('symbol')}" for row in report.get('changed_functions') or []
                 if isinstance(row, dict) and isinstance(row.get('file'), str) and not is_test_file(row['file'])}
    symbols = {name for name in report.get('changed_symbols') or []
               if isinstance(name, str) and not is_test_file(name.split('#', 1)[0])}
    return bool(functions) and all(reasons.get(name) == DOCS_ONLY for name in functions) and symbols <= functions


def stopped(report):
    side = report.get('side_by_side') if isinstance(report.get('side_by_side'), dict) else {}
    return bool(side.get('stopped')) or any(str(gap).startswith(CUT) for gap in report.get('gaps') or [])


def own_tests(report):
    """Tests the pull request adds or edits that ran on the head: replayed and not skipped there, or, with nothing
    replayed, changed functions in test files."""
    replayed = [row for row in report.get('replayed') or [] if isinstance(row, dict)]
    if replayed:
        return sum(row.get('head') != 'skipped' for row in replayed)
    return sum(isinstance(row, dict) and is_test_file(str(row.get('file', ''))) for row in report.get('changed_functions') or [])


def quiet_body(report, meta, first, extra):
    """Nothing found: the first line, and what ran and what was not seen, collapsed."""
    full = render(report, meta, extra='', quiet=False).split('\n', 1)[1].rsplit(MARKER, 1)[0].strip()
    return '\n'.join([first, '', '<details><summary>What ran and what was not seen</summary>', '', full, '', '</details>',
                      extra, MARKER]).replace('\n\n\n', '\n\n')


def extras(report, listed=LISTED):
    """Sections for features still behind a flag: renames and moves, and inputs on which two versions differ."""
    out = []
    moved = [row for row in report.get('refactors') or [] if isinstance(row, dict)]
    if moved and not report.get('error'):
        out += [f'### Renamed or moved, nothing else ({len(moved)})', '',
                'The same code under a new name or in a new place: refactor, behaviour preserved if tests pass.', '']
        out += rows(moved, lambda row: f"{code(row.get('from', '?'), 120)} -> {code(row.get('to', '?'), 120)} ({row.get('kind', '?')})",
                    listed) + ['']
    differ = [row for row in (report.get('equivalence') or {}).get('rows') or [] if isinstance(row, dict)]
    if differ and not report.get('error'):
        out += [f'### An input on which the two versions differ ({len(differ)})', '',
                'Found by a search over the inputs of annotated, pure changed functions (CrossHair, Hypothesis):', '']
        out += rows(differ, lambda row: f"{code(row.get('target', '?'), 120)}: {code(row.get('input', ''), 200)} gives "
                                        f"{code(row.get('before', ''), 160)} and {code(row.get('after', ''), 160)} "
                                        f"({row.get('tool', '?')})", listed) + ['']
    return out


def nothing_found(report):
    executed = report.get('executed') or {}
    counted, _ = split_flips(report)
    return (not report.get('error') and not report.get('failure') and report.get('flips') is not None and not counted
            and executed.get('ran') and reach(report)[0] is not False
            and not any(report.get(k) for k in ('change_evidence', 'behaviour_differences', 'generated_differences', 'unstable', 'cut',
                                                'refactors'))
            and not (report.get('equivalence') or {}).get('rows') and not (report.get('mutation') or {}).get('survivors')
            and not any(isinstance(r, dict) and not str(r.get('label', '')).startswith('fails') for r in report.get('flip_trust') or []))


def render(report, meta, limit=LIMIT, listed=LISTED, extra='', verify=None, quiet=False):
    if quiet and nothing_found(report):
        body = render(report, meta, limit, listed, '', verify)
        return quiet_body(report, meta, body.splitlines()[0], extra)
    head, base = meta.get('head'), meta.get('merge_base') or meta.get('base')
    executed = report.get('executed') or {}
    ran = executed.get('ran') or 0
    flips = report.get('flips')
    failures, updated = split_flips(report)
    aborted = report.get('failure')
    if report.get('error'):
        first = f"**AMU: no flip count** at {short(head)}: {code(report['error'])}"
    elif report.get('refactor_only'):
        moved = [row for row in report.get('refactors') or [] if isinstance(row, dict)]
        first = (f"**AMU: refactor only** at {short(head)}: every change renames or moves "
                 f"{plural(len(moved), 'definition')} without changing it; no tests run")
    elif aborted:
        first = f'**AMU: no flip count** at {short(head)}: the test runner aborts on the head before any test'
    elif flips is None or not ran:
        first = f'**AMU: no flip count** at {short(head)}: no candidate test ran'
    elif failures:
        first = f"**AMU: {plural(len(failures), 'flip')}** at {short(head)}, among {plural(ran, 'test')} run"
    elif report.get('adds_only'):
        # Only new definitions outside the tests: nothing that ran before changed. The new tests failing before the
        # change on the missing names is what they should do.
        replayed = [row for row in report.get('replayed') or [] if isinstance(row, dict)]
        made = [row for row in replayed if row.get('verdict') == 'new_code']
        kinds = sorted({str(row.get('why', '')).split(' on ', 1)[0] for row in made if row.get('why')}) or ['ImportError']
        first = f'**AMU: adds new code only** at {short(head)}'
        if made:
            verb = 'fails' if len(made) == 1 else 'fail'
            first += f"; its {plural(len(made), 'new test')} {verb} on the base with {' or '.join(kinds)}, as expected"
        elif not any(row.get('head') not in (None, 'skipped') for row in replayed):
            first += '; no test of it ran'
    elif docs_only(report) and not report.get('change_evidence'):
        # Sympy #30838, Django #22046: a docstring typo read "whether any ran the changed code was not seen".
        first = f"**AMU: docstring or comment changes only** at {short(head)}; no flip among {plural(ran, 'test')} run"
    else:
        reached, files = reach(report)
        if reached is False:
            # Never folded away: a reviewer reading only this line must not take it for "nothing changed".
            mine = own_tests(report)
            where = ', '.join(code(f, 120) for f in files[:3]) + (f' and {len(files) - 3} more' if len(files) > 3 else '')
            besides = f", apart from the {plural(mine, 'test')} this pull request adds or edits" if mine else ''
            first = f"**AMU: no test ran the changed code in {where}** at {short(head)}{besides}; {plural(ran, 'test')} run"
        elif reached:
            first = f"**AMU: 0 flips** at {short(head)}, among {plural(ran, 'test')} run, some of them on the changed code"
        else:
            first = (f"**AMU: no flip** at {short(head)} among {plural(ran, 'test')} run; whether any ran the changed code "
                     'was not seen')
    timed = report.get('side_by_side') if isinstance(report.get('side_by_side'), dict) else None
    if timed is not None and stopped(report) and not report.get('error') and not report.get('refactor_only'):
        first += (f"; side-by-side got to {timed.get('functions_called', 0)} of {timed.get('targets', 0)} changed "
                  'functions before its time limit')
    if report.get('cut') and not report.get('error'):
        cap = meta.get('wall_cap')
        cap = f' of {cap} s' if isinstance(cap, int) and not isinstance(cap, bool) and 0 < cap < 10**7 else ''
        first += f'; stopped at the wall cap{cap} before it finished'
    evidence = [row for row in report.get('change_evidence') or [] if isinstance(row, dict) and row.get('id')]
    if evidence and not report.get('error'):
        first += f"; {plural(len(evidence), 'test')} of the pull request's own fail on the merge base and pass on the head"
    behaviour = [row for row in report.get('behaviour_differences') or [] if isinstance(row, dict)]
    side = report.get('side_by_side') if isinstance(report.get('side_by_side'), dict) else None
    if behaviour and side is not None and not report.get('error'):
        first += f"; {plural(len(behaviour), 'behaviour difference')} on captured input, collapsed at the end"
    out, collapsed = [first, ''], []
    if failures and not report.get('error'):
        out += [f'### Flips ({len(failures)})', '',
                f'Pass on the merge base {short(base)}, fail on the head. Each was rerun on the merge base to confirm '
                'it passed there, and failed again on the head in every rerun made: in the same process, alone in a fresh '
                'process, and after the tests that ran before it, unless its row says it is order-dependent. A rerun that was '
                'not made is named on its row.', '']
        missing = {row.get('id'): [leg for leg, state in (row.get('reruns') or {}).items() if state is None]
                   for row in report.get('flip_trust') or [] if isinstance(row, dict)}
        leaks = {row.get('id'): row.get('why', '') for row in report.get('flip_trust') or [] if isinstance(row, dict)
                 and row.get('label') == 'fails: order-dependent, new with this change'}
        routes = {row.get('id'): row for row in report.get('flip_trust') or [] if isinstance(row, dict)}

        def short_id(ident):
            path, _, qual = str(ident).partition('#')
            return (qual or path.rsplit('/', 1)[-1]) if qual else path.rsplit('/', 1)[-1]

        def route(ident):
            row = routes.get(ident) or {}
            parts = []
            if isinstance(row.get('path'), list) and row['path']:
                parts.append('path ' + code(' > '.join(short_id(step) for step in row['path'][-6:]), 200))
            raised = row.get('raised') if isinstance(row.get('raised'), dict) else None
            if raised and isinstance(raised.get('through'), list):
                parts.append(code(raised.get('exception', '?'), 60) + ' raised through '
                             + code(' > '.join(short_id(step) for step in raised['through'][:6]), 200))
            found = row.get('isolated') if isinstance(row.get('isolated'), dict) else None
            if found and isinstance(found.get('hunks'), list) and found['hunks']:
                places = ', '.join(f"hunk {h.get('hunk', '?')} of {h.get('of', '?')} in {code(h.get('file', '?'), 120)} "
                                   f"at line {h.get('start', '?')}" for h in found['hunks'][:3] if isinstance(h, dict))
                parts.append(('caused by ' if found.get('finished') else 'narrowed to, search cut short: ') + places)
            return ('; ' + '; '.join(parts)) if parts else ''
        names = dict(in_process='in the same process', fresh_process='alone in a fresh process', after_set='after the tests before it')

        def flip(row):
            label = row.get('label') if isinstance(row, dict) else None
            gone = [names.get(leg, str(leg)) for leg in missing.get(failure_id(row), [])]
            return (code(failure_id(row)) + (' (fails as the test was before it was edited)' if label == EDITED else '')
                    + (f" (order-dependent, new with this change: {code(leaks[failure_id(row)], 200)})" if failure_id(row) in leaks else '')
                    + route(failure_id(row))
                    + (f" (not rerun {', '.join(gone)})" if gone else ''))
        out += rows(failures, flip, listed) + ['']
        if verify and verify.get('checked'):
            out += [f"Rerun on the merge base in a fresh job: {verify.get('held', 0)} passed again, "
                    f"{verify.get('false', 0)} failed there too, so not the change, "
                    f"{verify.get('other', 0)} could not be rerun.", '']
    if updated and not report.get('error'):
        out += [f'### Tests this pull request updated ({len(updated)})', '',
                'Pass on the merge base and fail on the head as they were before this pull request edited them; as edited, '
                'they pass. The edit is in the diff, so they are not flips.', '']
        out += rows(updated, lambda row: code(failure_id(row)), listed) + ['']
    if side is not None and not report.get('error'):
        section = [f"Each changed function the tests called on the merge base ran there twice as it was and twice as changed, "
                   f"on copies of the same arguments: {side.get('compared_calls', 0)} call(s) of "
                   f"{side.get('functions_called', 0)} of {side.get('targets', 0)} comparable changed function(s). Only "
                   'differences both versions repeat are listed.', '']

        def flat(side_result, field):
            value = side_result.get(field) if isinstance(side_result, dict) else None
            text = '?' if value is None else value if isinstance(value, str) else json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False)
            return re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text).replace('`', "'").strip()

        def difference(row):
            differs = [str(f) for f in row.get('differs') or []]
            # Show the first field that differs, cut to a window around where the two versions part: outcomes that
            # share a long prefix would otherwise both be cut before the part that differs.
            field = next((f for f in differs if f in ('result', 'args_after', 'stdout', 'calls')), 'result')
            was, now = flat(row.get('before'), field), flat(row.get('after'), field)
            at = next((i for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(was, now)) if a != b), min(len(was), len(now)))
            start = max(0, at - 40)

            def window(text):
                return ('…' if start else '') + text[start:start + 160] + ('…' if len(text) > start + 160 else '')
            where = f", from character {at + 1}" if start else ''
            return (f"{code(row.get('target', '?'), 120)} on {code(row.get('input', ''), 160)}: as it was {code(window(was), 170)}, "
                    f"as changed {code(window(now), 170)} (differs in: {code(', '.join(differs), 60)}; shown: {field}{where})")
        section += rows(behaviour, difference, listed) + ['']
        if behaviour:
            collapsed = [f'<details><summary>Behaviour differs on captured input ({len(behaviour)})</summary>', '',
                         "Collapsed until side-by-side's false rows are fixed: of 18 such rows hand-labelled on Django and "
                         'sympy pull requests, 11 were real differences and 7 came from how side-by-side runs the changed code.',
                         '', *section, '</details>', '']
        else:
            out += ['### Behaviour differs on captured input (0)', '', *section]
    made = report.get('generated') if isinstance(report.get('generated'), dict) else None
    produced = [row for row in report.get('generated_differences') or [] if isinstance(row, dict)]
    if made is not None and not report.get('error') and made.get('proposed'):
        out += [f"### Generated tests showing a difference ({len(produced)})", '']
        spent = (f"through {code(str(made.get('backend')), 20)}, at a cost of Claude plan usage, within "
                 f"{float(made.get('minutes_cap') or 0):g} min" if made.get('cost_basis') == 'plan usage' else
                 f"at ${float(made.get('cost') or 0):.3f} of a ${float(made.get('dollars_cap') or 0):.2f} cap")
        out += [f"For changed functions no test called, {code(made.get('model', '?'), 40)} proposed "
                f"{made.get('proposed', 0)} probe(s) for {made.get('functions', 0)} function(s), {spent}. Each was kept only if it "
                f"compiled ({made.get('compiled', 0)}), ran on the head ({made.get('ran', 0)}), gave the same outcome five times "

        if skipped_one:

def load(folder):
    folder = Path(folder)

    def read(name):
        try:
            value = json.loads((folder/name).read_text())
            return value if isinstance(value, dict) else {}
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            return {}
    report = read('report.json') or dict(error='no report.json in the artifact')
    return report, read('meta.json')


def load_verify(folder):
    """The fresh-job rerun's counts, as integers only; None when there are none."""
    try:
        value = json.loads((Path(folder)/'verify.json').read_text())
    except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
        return None
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        return None
    counts = {key: value.get(key) for key in ('checked', 'held', 'false', 'other')}
    if not all(isinstance(n, int) and not isinstance(n, bool) and 0 <= n < 10**7 for n in counts.values()):
        return None
    return counts

"""Tests that would catch a raise, missed: for one change, the tests that fail when its changed lines raise, less the
tests AMU had as candidates on the head.

Usage: python raise_missed.py --head TREE --patch PATCH --report REPORT.json --python PY [--runner pytest|django-runtests]
       [--workers N]

Each hunk's first changed statement on the head gets ``raise RuntimeError('AMU-RAISE <path>:<line>')`` in front of it,
at its indentation; a statement that starts a definition gets it as the first line of its body instead, so it raises
when called. Statements at module or class level are not given one (a raise at import fails every test importing the
module, which says nothing about one line); they are counted under ``not_injected``. Then the whole suite runs once on
the head copy with every raise in place, and a test that fails with the marker in its failure text is a catcher. A raise
in one hunk can keep another from running in the same test, so the catchers are a lower bound per hunk; their union is
what is compared.

Prints JSON: catchers, candidates, missed (catchers not among the candidates), and per hunk where its raise went.
"""
import argparse
import ast
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from pathlib import Path

MARK = 'AMU-RAISE'


def hunks(patch):
    """{path: [first added line of each hunk]} for production .py files, from a unified diff."""
    found, path, new_line, first = {}, None, 0, None
    for line in patch.splitlines():
        if line.startswith('+++ '):
            raw = line[4:].split('\t')[0]
            path = raw[2:] if raw.startswith('b/') else None if raw == '/dev/null' else raw
            if path and (not path.endswith('.py') or re.search(r'(^|/)(tests?|testing)/|(^|/)test_[^/]*\.py$|_test\.py$|conftest\.py$', path)):
                path = None
        elif line.startswith('@@') and path:
            new_line = int(re.match(r'@@ -\d+(?:,\d+)? \+(\d+)', line)[1])
            first = None
        elif path and line.startswith('+') and not line.startswith('+++'):
            if first is None:
                first = new_line
                found.setdefault(path, []).append(new_line)
            new_line += 1
        elif path and line.startswith(' '):
            new_line += 1
    return found


def inject(text, lines, path):
    """``text`` with a raise before the first statement starting on or after each of ``lines`` within its hunk."""
    tree = ast.parse(text)
    statements = []
    parents = {}
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):
            parents[child] = node
        if isinstance(node, ast.stmt):
            statements.append(node)
    rows, where = text.splitlines(True), []
    inserts = {}
    for line in lines:
        hit = sorted((s for s in statements if s.lineno >= line), key=lambda s: (s.lineno, -s.col_offset))
        if not hit or hit[0].lineno > line + 30:
            where.append(dict(line=line, at=None, why='no statement'))
            continue
        node = hit[0]
        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
            body = node.body[0]
            if isinstance(body, ast.Expr) and isinstance(getattr(body, 'value', None), ast.Constant) and len(node.body) > 1:
                body = node.body[1]

        inserts[node.lineno] = f"{indent}raise RuntimeError('{MARK} {path}:{line}')\n"
        where.append(dict(line=line, at=node.lineno))
    for at in sorted(inserts, reverse=True):
        rows.insert(at - 1, inserts[at])
    return ''.join(rows), where

    command = [python, '-m', 'pytest', '-q', '-p', 'no:cacheprovider', '-p', 'no:randomly', f'--junitxml={report}']
    if workers > 1:
        command += ['-n', str(workers)]

    for case in ET.parse(report).getroot().iter('testcase'):

        if MARK not in said:
            continue
        parts = case.get('classname', '').split('.')
        for cut in range(len(parts), 0, -1):
            if (tree/('/'.join(parts[:cut]) + '.py')).is_file():
                found.add('::'.join(['/'.join(parts[:cut]) + '.py', *parts[cut:], case.get('name', '').split('[')[0]]))
                break
    return found


def catchers_django(python, tree, workers):

                          capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=6 * 3600)
    output = done.stdout + done.stderr
    found = set()

        match = re.search(r'^(?:ERROR|FAIL): (\w+) \(([\w.]+)\)', block, re.M)

        parts = label.split('.')
        for cut in range(len(parts) - 1, 0, -1):
            if (tree/'tests'/('/'.join(parts[:cut]) + '.py')).is_file():
                found.add('::'.join(['tests/' + '/'.join(parts[:cut]) + '.py', *parts[cut:]]))
                break
    return found


def main(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument('--head', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--patch', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--report', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--python', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--runner', default='pytest')
    p.add_argument('--workers', type=int, default=1)
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    patch = Path(args.patch).read_text()
    report = json.loads(Path(args.report).read_text())
    candidates = set(report.get('candidate_sources') or {}) or {row['id'] for row in report.get('tests') or []}
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='amu-raise-') as scratch:
        tree = Path(scratch)/'tree'
        shutil.copytree(args.head, tree, symlinks=True, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns('.git', '.amu', '__pycache__'))
        placed = {}
        for path, lines in hunks(patch).items():
            text = (tree/path).read_text()
            changed, where = inject(text, lines, path)
            (tree/path).write_text(changed)
            placed[path] = where
        injected = sum(1 for rows in placed.values() for row in rows if row.get('at'))
        if args.runner == 'django-runtests':
            caught = catchers_django(args.python, tree, args.workers)
        else:
            caught = catchers_pytest(args.python, tree, args.workers, Path(scratch)/'raise.xml')
    missed = sorted(caught - candidates)
    print(json.dumps(dict(injected=injected, not_injected=sum(1 for rows in placed.values() for row in rows if not row.get('at')),
                          catchers=len(caught), candidates=len(candidates), missed=len(missed), missed_tests=missed[:50],
                          placed=placed), indent=1))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

  the code before the change, the added lines on the code after it.

  tests seen entering the changed code, from this run or a recording kept for the same commit; the static graph

beside a stub, a src/ layout, a name looked up at run time, inheritance). Execution evidence is now primary:

- record (new): a sys.monitoring recorder loaded as sitecustomize in each side's own test run. Per test, the
  watched lines it ran; per call into a watched function, digests of its input (structure and state, slots
  included, never repr or __eq__ of project objects) and of its output or exception.
- hunks (new): each changed hunk with the lines that tell whether a test ran it: the enclosing function's body on
  the code before the change, the added lines on the code after it.
- evidence (new): the code before the change runs first, recorded. When the suite's last measured time fits the
  budget, or none was measured, that is the whole suite (pytest's testpaths respected), and if it finishes in
  its share the code after the change runs the whole suite too: no selection. Otherwise the candidates are the
  tests seen entering the changed code, from this run or a recording kept for the same commit; the static graph
  adds candidates only for hunks no recording speaks for. Every candidate runs on both sides; the report says
  where each came from (candidate_sources, selection_evidence) and which tests ran each hunk (hunks).

- runners: pytest 9's native [tool.pytest] table is read; one split half failing like the whole batch no longer
  marks every candidate unrunnable (two disjoint halves must); unrunnable candidates are named in the report.

went from 8 missed of 8 (static selection) to 0 missed of 8.

"""Behaviour differences from paired records: each side's calls recorded in its own run, compared on equal inputs."""
import difflib
import subprocess
import sys
import textwrap

import pytest

from amu.core import analyze

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(sys.version_info < (3, 12), reason='sys.monitoring needs Python 3.12')


def change(tmp_path, before, after, **kwargs):
    for name, text in before.items():
        (tmp_path/name).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (tmp_path/name).write_text(text)
    for args in (['init', '-q'], ['add', '-A'], ['-c', 'user.name=t', '-c', 'user.email=t@t', 'commit', '-qm', 'base']):
        subprocess.run(['git', *args], cwd=tmp_path, check=True, capture_output=True)
    for name, text in after.items():
        (tmp_path/name).write_text(text)
    diff = ''.join(''.join(difflib.unified_diff(before.get(n, '').splitlines(True), after[n].splitlines(True), 'a/' + n, 'b/' + n))
                   for n in after if before.get(n) != after[n])
    return analyze(tmp_path, diff, full_evidence=True, index_dir=tmp_path/'.index', run=True, python=sys.executable, **kwargs)


# A slotted class gains a field its constructor sets, and a method reads it. On the code after the change every object
# has the field; on the code before it none has. Running the new method on an object the old code built raises
# AttributeError: that is how side-by-side read it. No real call does that.
SLOTTED0 = textwrap.dedent('''\
    class Field:
        __slots__ = ("name", "alias")

        def __init__(self, name, alias=None):
            self.name = name
            self.alias = alias or name

        def renamed(self, name):
            return Field(name, None if self.alias == self.name else self.alias)
    ''')
SLOTTED1 = textwrap.dedent('''\
    class Field:
        __slots__ = ("name", "alias", "alias_is_default")

        def __init__(self, name, alias=None):
            self.name = name
            self.alias = alias or name
            self.alias_is_default = alias is None

        def renamed(self, name):
            return Field(name, None if self.alias_is_default else self.alias)
    ''')
TESTS = textwrap.dedent('''\
    from lib import Field


    def test_renamed_follows_a_default_alias():
        assert Field("a").renamed("b").alias == "b"


    def test_renamed_keeps_an_explicit_alias():
        assert Field("a", "x").renamed("b").alias == "x"
    ''')


def test_a_slotted_class_gaining_a_field_gives_no_false_row(tmp_path):
    report = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': SLOTTED0, 'tests/test_lib.py': TESTS}, {'lib.py': SLOTTED1})
    assert report['side_by_side']['mode'] == 'paired records', report['side_by_side']
    assert report['behaviour_differences'] == [], report['behaviour_differences']
    # The objects differ (one has a field the other lacks), so their calls are not compared: counted, not guessed.
    assert report['side_by_side']['inputs_differ'] >= 1, report['side_by_side']


def test_the_old_mode_still_gives_the_false_rows_it_gave_and_is_behind_a_flag(tmp_path):
    report = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': SLOTTED0, 'tests/test_lib.py': TESTS}, {'lib.py': SLOTTED1},
                    extras=('sidebyside-legacy',))
    assert report['side_by_side'].get('mode') != 'paired records'
    raised = [row for row in report['behaviour_differences'] if row['after']['result'][0] == 'raise']
    assert raised, report['behaviour_differences']  # the error this replaces


def test_a_real_difference_on_an_equal_input_is_a_row(tmp_path):
    lib0 = 'def clamp(v, top=10):\n    return min(v, top)\n'
    lib1 = 'def clamp(v, top=10):\n    return min(v, top - 1)\n'
    tests = 'from lib import clamp\n\n\ndef test_big():\n    assert clamp(50) > 0\n'
    report = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': lib0, 'tests/test_lib.py': tests}, {'lib.py': lib1})
    [row] = report['behaviour_differences']
    assert row['target'] == 'lib.py#clamp' and row['test'] == 'tests/test_lib.py::test_big', row
    assert row['before']['result'][0] == ['return', '10'] and row['after']['result'][0] == ['return', '9'], row
    from amu.ci.render import render
    body = render(report, dict(head='a' * 40, merge_base='b' * 40))
    assert body.splitlines()[0].endswith('; 1 behaviour difference on the same input'), body

"""Behaviour differences from paired records: each side's calls recorded in its own run, compared on equal inputs."""
import difflib
import subprocess
import sys
import textwrap

import pytest

from amu.core import analyze

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(sys.version_info < (3, 12), reason='sys.monitoring needs Python 3.12')


def change(tmp_path, before, after, **kwargs):
    for name, text in before.items():
        (tmp_path/name).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (tmp_path/name).write_text(text)
    for args in (['init', '-q'], ['add', '-A'], ['-c', 'user.name=t', '-c', 'user.email=t@t', 'commit', '-qm', 'base']):
        subprocess.run(['git', *args], cwd=tmp_path, check=True, capture_output=True)
    for name, text in after.items():
        (tmp_path/name).write_text(text)
    diff = ''.join(''.join(difflib.unified_diff(before.get(n, '').splitlines(True), after[n].splitlines(True), 'a/' + n, 'b/' + n))
                   for n in after if before.get(n) != after[n])
    return analyze(tmp_path, diff, full_evidence=True, index_dir=tmp_path/'.index', run=True, python=sys.executable, **kwargs)


# A slotted class gains a field its constructor sets, and a method reads it. On the code after the change every object
# has the field; on the code before it none has. Running the new method on an object the old code built raises
# AttributeError: that is how the old side-by-side read it. No real call does that.
SLOTTED0 = textwrap.dedent('''\
    class Field:
        __slots__ = ("name", "alias")

        def __init__(self, name, alias=None):
            self.name = name
            self.alias = alias or name

        def renamed(self, name):
            return Field(name, None if self.alias == self.name else self.alias)
    ''')
SLOTTED1 = textwrap.dedent('''\
    class Field:
        __slots__ = ("name", "alias", "alias_is_default")

        def __init__(self, name, alias=None):
            self.name = name
            self.alias = alias or name
            self.alias_is_default = alias is None

        def renamed(self, name):
            return Field(name, None if self.alias_is_default else self.alias)
    ''')
TESTS = textwrap.dedent('''\
    from lib import Field


    def test_renamed_follows_a_default_alias():
        assert Field("a").renamed("b").alias == "b"


    def test_renamed_keeps_an_explicit_alias():
        assert Field("a", "x").renamed("b").alias == "x"
    ''')


def test_a_slotted_class_gaining_a_field_gives_no_false_row(tmp_path):
    report = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': SLOTTED0, 'tests/test_lib.py': TESTS}, {'lib.py': SLOTTED1})
    assert report['side_by_side']['mode'] == 'paired records', report['side_by_side']
    assert report['behaviour_differences'] == [], report['behaviour_differences']
    # The objects differ (one has a field the other lacks), so their calls are not compared: counted, not guessed.
    assert report['side_by_side']['inputs_differ'] >= 1, report['side_by_side']


def test_the_old_mode_is_behind_a_flag(tmp_path):
    report = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': SLOTTED0, 'tests/test_lib.py': TESTS}, {'lib.py': SLOTTED1},
                    extras=('sidebyside-legacy',))
    assert report['side_by_side'].get('mode') != 'paired records'
    # Old mode: the changed methods run on objects the old code built; its set-aside rules decide what is shown.
    assert 'input_built_before_the_change' in report['side_by_side'], report['side_by_side']

    lib1 = 'def clamp(v, top=10):\n    return min(v, top - 1)\n'
    tests = 'from lib import clamp\n\n\ndef test_big():\n    assert clamp(50) > 0\n'

    [row] = report['behaviour_differences']
    assert row['target'] == 'lib.py#clamp' and row['test'] == 'tests/test_lib.py::test_big', row
    assert row['before']['result'] == ['return', '10'] and row['after']['result'] == ['return', '9'], row
    from amu.ci.render import render

    assert body.splitlines()[0].endswith('; 1 behaviour difference on the same input'), body
    assert '### Behaviour differs on the same input (1)' in body, body


def test_a_difference_neither_side_repeats_is_not_a_row(tmp_path):
    lib0 = 'import random\n\n\ndef noisy(x):\n    return random.random() + x\n'

    assert report['side_by_side']['unstable'] == 1, report['side_by_side']

"""Behaviour differences from paired records: each side's calls recorded in its own run, compared on equal inputs."""
import difflib
import subprocess
import sys
import textwrap

import pytest

from amu.core import analyze

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(sys.version_info < (3, 12), reason='sys.monitoring needs Python 3.12')


def change(tmp_path, before, after, **kwargs):
    for name, text in before.items():
        (tmp_path/name).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (tmp_path/name).write_text(text)
    for args in (['init', '-q'], ['add', '-A'], ['-c', 'user.name=t', '-c', 'user.email=t@t', 'commit', '-qm', 'base']):
        subprocess.run(['git', *args], cwd=tmp_path, check=True, capture_output=True)
    for name, text in after.items():
        (tmp_path/name).write_text(text)
    diff = ''.join(''.join(difflib.unified_diff(before.get(n, '').splitlines(True), after[n].splitlines(True), 'a/' + n, 'b/' + n))
                   for n in after if before.get(n) != after[n])
    return analyze(tmp_path, diff, full_evidence=True, index_dir=tmp_path/'.index', run=True, python=sys.executable, **kwargs)


# A slotted class gains a field its constructor sets, and a method reads it. On the code after the change every object
# has the field; on the code before it none has. Running the new method on an object the old code built raises
# AttributeError: that is how the old side-by-side read it. No real call does that.
SLOTTED0 = textwrap.dedent('''\
    class Field:
        __slots__ = ("name", "alias")

        def __init__(self, name, alias=None):
            self.name = name
            self.alias = alias or name

        def renamed(self, name):
            return Field(name, None if self.alias == self.name else self.alias)
    ''')
SLOTTED1 = textwrap.dedent('''\
    class Field:
        __slots__ = ("name", "alias", "alias_is_default")

        def __init__(self, name, alias=None):
            self.name = name
            self.alias = alias or name
            self.alias_is_default = alias is None

        def renamed(self, name):
            return Field(name, None if self.alias_is_default else self.alias)
    ''')
TESTS = textwrap.dedent('''\
    from lib import Field


    def test_renamed_follows_a_default_alias():
        assert Field("a").renamed("b").alias == "b"


    def test_renamed_keeps_an_explicit_alias():
        assert Field("a", "x").renamed("b").alias == "x"
    ''')


def test_a_slotted_class_gaining_a_field_gives_no_false_row(tmp_path):
    report = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': SLOTTED0, 'tests/test_lib.py': TESTS}, {'lib.py': SLOTTED1})
    assert report['side_by_side']['mode'] == 'paired records', report['side_by_side']
    assert report['behaviour_differences'] == [], report['behaviour_differences']
    # The objects differ (one has a field the other lacks), so their calls are not compared: counted, not guessed.
    assert report['side_by_side']['inputs_differ'] >= 1, report['side_by_side']


def test_the_old_mode_is_behind_a_flag(tmp_path):
    report = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': SLOTTED0, 'tests/test_lib.py': TESTS}, {'lib.py': SLOTTED1},
                    extras=('sidebyside-legacy',))
    assert report['side_by_side'].get('mode') != 'paired records'
    # Old mode: the changed methods run on objects the old code built; its set-aside rules decide what is shown.
    assert 'input_built_before_the_change' in report['side_by_side'], report['side_by_side']


def test_a_real_difference_on_an_equal_input_is_a_row(tmp_path):
    lib0 = 'def clamp(v, top=10):\n    return min(v, top)\n'
    lib1 = 'def clamp(v, top=10):\n    return min(v, top - 1)\n'
    tests = 'from lib import clamp\n\n\ndef test_big():\n    assert clamp(50) > 0\n'
    report = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': lib0, 'tests/test_lib.py': tests}, {'lib.py': lib1})
    [row] = report['behaviour_differences']
    assert row['target'] == 'lib.py#clamp' and row['test'] == 'tests/test_lib.py::test_big', row
    assert row['before']['result'] == ['return', '10'] and row['after']['result'] == ['return', '9'], row
    from amu.ci.render import render
    body = render(report, dict(head='a' * 40, merge_base='b' * 40))
    assert body.splitlines()[0].endswith('; 1 behaviour difference on the same input'), body
    assert '### Behaviour differs on the same input (1)' in body, body


def test_a_difference_neither_side_repeats_is_not_a_row(tmp_path):
    lib0 = 'import random\n\n\ndef noisy(x):\n    return random.random() + x\n'
    lib1 = 'import random\n\n\ndef noisy(x):\n    return random.random() + x + 0\n'
    tests = 'from lib import noisy\n\n\ndef test_noisy():\n    assert noisy(1) >= 1\n'
    report = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': lib0, 'tests/test_lib.py': tests}, {'lib.py': lib1})
    assert report['behaviour_differences'] == [], report['behaviour_differences']
    assert report['side_by_side']['unstable'] == 1, report['side_by_side']

"""The first line from per-hunk evidence states: the worst hunk is what it reports; every hunk is listed."""
import difflib
import subprocess
import sys
import textwrap

import pytest

from amu.ci.render import render
from amu.core import analyze

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(sys.version_info < (3, 12), reason='sys.monitoring needs Python 3.12')
HERE = f'{sys.version_info[0]}.{sys.version_info[1]}'

LIB = textwrap.dedent('''\
    def area(w, h):
        """Area of a w by h box."""
        # width times height
        return w * h


    def volume(w, h, d):
        return area(w, h) * d
    ''')
TESTS = 'from lib import area, volume\n\n\ndef test_area():\n    assert area(2, 3) == 6\n\n\ndef test_volume():\n    assert volume(1, 2, 3) == 6\n'


def change(tmp_path, before, after):
    for name, text in before.items():
        (tmp_path/name).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (tmp_path/name).write_text(text)
    for args in (['init', '-q'], ['add', '-A'], ['-c', 'user.name=t', '-c', 'user.email=t@t', 'commit', '-qm', 'base']):
        subprocess.run(['git', *args], cwd=tmp_path, check=True, capture_output=True)
    for name, text in after.items():
        (tmp_path/name).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (tmp_path/name).write_text(text)
    diff = ''.join(''.join(difflib.unified_diff(before.get(n, '').splitlines(True), after[n].splitlines(True), 'a/' + n, 'b/' + n))
                   for n in after if before.get(n) != after[n])
    report = analyze(tmp_path, diff, full_evidence=True, index_dir=tmp_path/'.index', run=True, python=sys.executable)
    return report, render(report, dict(head='a' * 40, merge_base='b' * 40)).splitlines()


def test_a_comment_typo_is_not_code(tmp_path):
    report, body = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': LIB, 'tests/test_lib.py': TESTS}, {'lib.py': LIB.replace('width times', 'width by')})
    assert [row['state'] for row in report['hunks']] == ['not-code'], report['hunks']
    assert body[0].startswith('**AMU: docstring or comment changes only**'), body[0]


def test_a_docstring_edit_beside_a_new_function_is_new_code_only(tmp_path):
    after = LIB.replace('Area of a w by h box.', 'Area of a box, w by h.') + '\n\ndef perimeter(w, h):\n    return 2 * (w + h)\n'
    report, body = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': LIB, 'tests/test_lib.py': TESTS}, {'lib.py': after})
    assert sorted(row['state'] for row in report['hunks']) == ['new-code', 'not-code'], report['hunks']
    assert body[0].startswith('**AMU: adds new code only**'), body[0]


def test_a_new_function_existing_code_calls_is_not_new_code(tmp_path):
    after = LIB.replace('return area(w, h) * d', 'return base(w, h) * d') + '\n\ndef base(w, h):\n    return area(w, h)\n'
    report, body = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': LIB, 'tests/test_lib.py': TESTS}, {'lib.py': after})
    assert 'new-code' not in [row['state'] for row in report['hunks']], report['hunks']
    assert 'adds new code' not in body[0], body[0]


def test_every_hunk_ran_on_both_sides(tmp_path):
    report, body = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': LIB, 'tests/test_lib.py': TESTS}, {'lib.py': LIB.replace('* d', '* d * 1')})
    assert [row['state'] for row in report['hunks']] == ['executed-both-sides'], report['hunks']
    assert body[0].endswith('ran all 2 tests; every changed hunk ran on both sides, in up to 1 test'), body[0]
    assert '### Changed hunks (1)' in body


def test_a_hunk_no_test_runs_is_named_in_the_first_line(tmp_path):
    lib = LIB + '\n\ndef unused(x):\n    return x + 1\n'
    report, body = change(tmp_path, {'lib.py': lib, 'tests/test_lib.py': TESTS}, {'lib.py': lib.replace('x + 1', 'x + 2')})
    assert [row['state'] for row in report['hunks']] == ['executed-none'], report['hunks']
    assert body[0].endswith('; 1 of 1 changed hunk ran in no test: `lib.py:13`'), body[0]


@pytest.mark.parametrize('guard,reason', [
    # The guard is a constant in another module, imported: the function runs only when it holds.
    ("import sys\nNEWER = sys.version_info[:2] >= (99, 0)\n", f'not executable on Python {HERE} here'),
    ("import sys\nNEWER = sys.platform == 'not-this-platform'\n", f'not executable on {sys.platform} here'),
    ("try:\n    import amu_no_such_module\n    NEWER = True\nexcept ImportError:\n    NEWER = False\n",
     'not executable on amu_no_such_module not installed here'),
])
def test_code_only_called_under_a_condition_false_here_cannot_run_here(tmp_path, guard, reason):
    lib = ('from compat import NEWER\n\n\ndef build(x):\n    if NEWER:\n        return replace(x)\n    return x\n\n\n'
           'def replace(x):\n    return x * 2\n')
    files = {'compat.py': guard, 'lib.py': lib, 'tests/test_lib.py': 'from lib import build\n\n\ndef test_build():\n    assert build(1)\n'}
    report, body = change(tmp_path, files, {'lib.py': lib.replace('x * 2', 'x * 3')})
    [row] = report['hunks']
    assert row['state'] == 'not-executable-here' and row['why'] == reason, row
    assert body[0].endswith(f'; 1 of 1 changed hunk {reason}: `lib.py:12`'), body[0]

"""Run the frozen 47 pull requests with an AMU engine checkout as the Action runs it, then the raise measure.

Usage: python run47.py --engine DIR --tag TAG [--extras E] [--only repo#n ...] [--no-raise]
Outputs under out-TAG/<repo>/<n>/: report.json, meta.json, patch.diff, comment.md, raise.json, timing.json.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

W = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FREEZE = Path('/Users/Abslock128/Documents/ChatGPT/AMU/fix-base/evaluation/performance-v042/freeze.json')
AMU_PY = str(W/'amuvenv'/'bin'/'python')
WORKERS = {'django': 8, 'sympy': 8, 'flask': 4}


def env_for(name, head):
    if name != 'flask':
        return name
    lock = (head/'uv.lock').read_text() if (head/'uv.lock').exists() else ''
    lines = lock.splitlines()
    pin = next((line.split('"')[1] for prev, line in zip(lines, lines[1:]) if prev == 'name = "pytest"'), '')
    major_minor = tuple(int(p) for p in pin.split('.')[:2]) if pin else (99, 0)
    return 'flask-p90' if major_minor < (9, 1) else 'flask'


def git(repo, *args):
    return subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo), *args], capture_output=True, text=True)


def one(engine, tag, name, pr, extras, measure):
    out = W/f'out-{tag}'/name/str(pr['number'])
    if (out/'timing.json').exists():
        return json.loads((out/'timing.json').read_text())
    shutil.rmtree(out, ignore_errors=True)
    out.mkdir(parents=True)
    clone = W/'repos'/name
    head = W/f'work-{tag}'/name/str(pr['number'])
    git(clone, 'worktree', 'remove', '--force', str(head))
    shutil.rmtree(head, ignore_errors=True)
    head.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if git(clone, 'cat-file', '-e', pr['head_sha']).returncode:
        git(clone, 'fetch', '-q', 'origin', pr['head_sha'])
    git(clone, 'worktree', 'add', '--detach', '-q', str(head), pr['head_sha'])
    python = str(W/'env'/env_for(name, head)/'bin'/'python')
    env = dict({k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith('ANTHROPIC_')}, PYTHONPATH=str(engine))
    command = [AMU_PY, '-P', '-m', 'amu.ci.run', '--base', pr['base_sha'], '--head', pr['head_sha'], '--out', str(out),
               '--python', python, '--pr', str(pr['number']), '--install-ok', 'true', '--amu-ref', tag,
               '--budget', '300', '--wall-cap', '1200', '--generate-dollars', '0', '--extras', extras]
    began = time.monotonic()
    done = subprocess.run(command, cwd=head, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    seconds = round(time.monotonic() - began, 1)
    (out/'run.log').write_text(done.stdout[-20000:] + done.stderr[-20000:])
    comment = subprocess.run([AMU_PY, '-P', '-m', 'amu.ci.render', str(out)], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env).stdout
    (out/'comment.md').write_text(comment)
    timing = dict(repo=name, number=pr['number'], seconds=seconds, first=(comment.splitlines() or [''])[0])
    if measure and (out/'report.json').exists() and (out/'patch.diff').exists():
        runner = 'django-runtests' if name == 'django' else 'pytest'
        raised = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(engine/'evaluation'/'generalize'/'raise_missed.py'), '--head', str(head),
                                 '--patch', str(out/'patch.diff'), '--report', str(out/'report.json'), '--python', python,
                                 '--runner', runner, '--workers', str(WORKERS[name])], capture_output=True, text=True)
        (out/'raise.json').write_text(raised.stdout or json.dumps(dict(error=raised.stderr[-3000:])))
    git(clone, 'worktree', 'remove', '--force', str(head))
    (out/'timing.json').write_text(json.dumps(timing))
    return timing


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument('--engine', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--tag', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--extras', default='')
    p.add_argument('--only', nargs='*')

# publish.yml, no environment). No PyPI token is stored here.
name: Publish to PyPI

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: Release tag to build and upload (for example v0.1.0).
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: publish-pypi
  cancel-in-progress: false

  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read

def test_a_directory_whose_conftest_cannot_load_does_not_take_the_other_tests_with_it(tmp_path):
    # Two parts split from the same failing part are not disjoint: only two parts with no test in common, both failing
    # alike, say the runner itself aborts.
    from amu.core import runners
    (tmp_path/'examples/tests').mkdir(parents=True)
    (tmp_path/'examples/tests/conftest.py').write_text('import not_installed_example\n')
    (tmp_path/'examples/tests/test_example.py').write_text('def test_one():\n    pass\n\n\ndef test_two():\n    pass\n')
    (tmp_path/'tests').mkdir()
    (tmp_path/'tests/test_good.py').write_text(''.join(f'def test_{n}():\n    pass\n\n\n' for n in range(6)))
    ids = ['examples/tests/test_example.py::test_one', 'examples/tests/test_example.py::test_two',
           *[f'tests/test_good.py::test_{n}' for n in range(6)]]
    found, problem = runners.execute(runners.get(tmp_path, 'pytest'), sys.executable, tmp_path, ids, tmp_path/'r.xml', 120)
    assert all(found[f'tests/test_good.py::test_{n}'] == 'passed' for n in range(6)), found

EOF

# AMU on pull requests: install note and sample comment

For the owner's introductions to maintainers of Python repositories with slow suites.

import re
import sys

    full = f'{ROOT}/{path}'

    changed = text.replace(f'v{OLD}', f'v{NEW}').replace(f'"{OLD}"', f'"{NEW}"')
    assert changed != text, path
    open(full, 'w').write(changed)

note = f'{ROOT}/evaluation/ci/INSTALL-NOTE.md'
text = open(note).read()
old = '''AMU runs the tests that a pull request's diff reaches on both sides of the change, the merge base and the head, and

new = '''AMU runs tests on both sides of a pull request, the merge base and the head, and posts one comment listing the tests
that flip from passing to failing. When the suite fits its budget it runs the whole suite on both sides; otherwise it
runs the tests it saw running the changed code on the merge base, and the static graph only for code no run covered.'''
assert old in text
text = text.replace(old, new)
old = '''`python -m pip install -e . pytest hypothesis`.'''
new = '''`python -m pip install -e . pytest hypothesis`. A project that keeps its test dependencies in `[dependency-groups]`

assert old in text
text = text.replace(old, new)
old = '''- It caches its index keyed on the merge base.'''

  platform, or with a module that is not installed) is listed as not executable here; set `python-version:` to the
  version the change is for.
- It caches its index, and what it recorded on the merge base, keyed on the merge base.'''
assert old in text
text = text.replace(old, new)
open(note, 'w').write(text)
print('release edits applied')

"""Replay upstream pull requests as pull requests on a fork, with the AMU workflows installed per the install note.

Usage: python replay.py --clone DIR --fork owner/name --list FILE.tsv --install CMD --prefix amu6 --upstream NAME
                        [--main] [--open]
FILE.tsv rows: number, merge base, head sha, title. Workflows come from ../rel/ci (the release's templates) with both
install lines set to CMD. --main commits them to the fork's default branch (the posting workflow runs only from
there). Each base branch is <prefix>-base-<merge base[:10]> = merge base + one commit adding the workflows; each head
branch is amu-pr-<n> = the pull request's own head commit. --open opens the pull requests through the REST API and
prints number, upstream number, created_at. Bodies name the upstream pull request without # or a link.
"""
import argparse
import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

W = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
NAME, EMAIL = 'abslock128w', 'rajesh.v@vmrcloudsolutions.com'
TRAILER = 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>'


def git(clone, *args, check=True):
    done = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(clone), *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and done.returncode:
        raise SystemExit(f'git {" ".join(args)}: {done.stderr}')
    return done.stdout.strip()


def workflows(install):
    out = {}
    for name in ('amu-pr.yml', 'amu-pr-comment.yml'):
        text = (W/'rel'/'ci'/name).read_text()
        if name == 'amu-pr.yml':
            text = text.replace('install: python -m pip install -e .', 'install: ' + install)
            assert text.count('install: ' + install) == 2, 'both install lines'
        out[name] = text
    return out


def commit_on(clone, start, files, message, branch):
    work = W/'replay-work'
    git(clone, 'worktree', 'remove', '--force', str(work), check=False)
    git(clone, 'worktree', 'add', '-q', '--detach', str(work), start)
    folder = work/'.github'/'workflows'
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for name, text in files.items():
        (folder/name).write_text(text)
    git(work, 'add', '.github/workflows/amu-pr.yml', '.github/workflows/amu-pr-comment.yml')
    git(work, '-c', f'user.name={NAME}', '-c', f'user.email={EMAIL}', 'commit', '-qm', message, '-m', TRAILER)
    git(work, 'branch', '-f', branch, 'HEAD')
    git(clone, 'worktree', 'remove', '--force', str(work))


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument('--clone', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--fork', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--list', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--install', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--prefix', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--upstream', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--main', action='store_true')
    p.add_argument('--open', action='store_true')
    a = p.parse_args()
    clone, files = Path(a.clone), workflows(a.install)
    rows = [line.rstrip('\n').split('\t') for line in Path(a.list).read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]
    git(clone, 'fetch', '-q', 'origin')
    if a.main:
        default = json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['gh', 'api', f'repos/{a.fork}', '--jq', '{b: .default_branch}']))['b']
        git(clone, 'fetch', '-q', 'fork', default, check=False)
        start = f'fork/{default}' if git(clone, 'rev-parse', '-q', '--verify', f'fork/{default}', check=False) else f'origin/{default}'
        commit_on(clone, start, files, 'Install the AMU pull request workflows (AMU v0.6.0) for a replay pilot on this fork',
                  'replay-main')
        git(clone, 'push', '-q', 'fork', f'replay-main:refs/heads/{default}')
    refs = []
    for number, base, head, *_ in rows:
        branch = f'{a.prefix}-base-{base[:10]}'
        commit_on(clone, base, files, f'Add the AMU pull request workflows (AMU v0.6.0) at merge base {base[:10]}', branch)
        git(clone, 'branch', '-f', f'amu-pr-{number}', head)
        refs += [f'refs/heads/{branch}:refs/heads/{branch}', f'refs/heads/amu-pr-{number}:refs/heads/amu-pr-{number}']
    git(clone, 'push', '-q', '-f', 'fork', *sorted(set(refs)))
    if a.open:
        for number, base, head, title, *_ in rows:
            body = (f'Replay of upstream {a.upstream} pull request {number}, for an AMU v0.6.0 pilot on this fork. Base: the '
                    f'upstream merge base {base[:10]} plus one commit adding the AMU workflows. Head: the pull request\'s own '
                    'commits. Not for merging.')
            made = json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['gh', 'api', f'repos/{a.fork}/pulls', '-f', f'title=Replay {number} (v0.6.0): {title.replace("#", "")}',
                                                       '-f', f'head=amu-pr-{number}', '-f', f'base={a.prefix}-base-{base[:10]}',
                                                       '-f', f'body={body}', '--jq', '{n: .number, at: .created_at}']))
            print(made['n'], number, made['at'], flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""Collect a fork pilot's live results: per pull request the AMU job time, open-to-comment time, the comment, and the
artifact (report.json, meta.json, patch.diff). Usage: python collect.py --fork owner/name --opened FILE --out DIR
FILE rows: fork PR number, upstream number, created_at (as printed by replay.py)."""
import argparse
import datetime as D
import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path


def api(path):
    return json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['gh', 'api', path]))


def when(text):
    return D.datetime.fromisoformat(text.replace('Z', '+00:00'))


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument('--fork', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--opened', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--out', required=True)
    a = p.parse_args()
    out = Path(a.out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rows = []
    for line in Path(a.opened).read_text().splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) < 3 or not parts[0].isdigit():
            continue
        fork_pr, upstream, created = (parts[1], parts[0], parts[2]) if len(parts) == 3 and parts[2].startswith('20') and int(parts[0]) > 999 and int(parts[1]) < 999 else parts[:3]
        rows.append((int(fork_pr), int(upstream), created))
    runs = api(f'repos/{a.fork}/actions/runs?per_page=100&event=pull_request')['workflow_runs']
    comments = []
    page = 1
    while True:
        got = api(f'repos/{a.fork}/issues/comments?per_page=100&page={page}')
        comments += got
        if len(got) < 100:
            break
        page += 1
    table = []
    for fork_pr, upstream, created in rows:
        pr = api(f'repos/{a.fork}/pulls/{fork_pr}')
        mine = [r for r in runs if r['name'] == 'AMU pull request' and r['head_sha'] == pr['head']['sha']
                and any(x['number'] == fork_pr for x in r.get('pull_requests') or [])] or \
               [r for r in runs if r['name'] == 'AMU pull request' and r['head_sha'] == pr['head']['sha'] and r['created_at'] >= created]
        run = sorted(mine, key=lambda r: r['created_at'])[-1] if mine else None
        jobs = api(f"repos/{a.fork}/actions/runs/{run['id']}/jobs")['jobs'] if run else []
        amu = next((j for j in jobs if j['name'] == 'amu' and j.get('completed_at')), None)
        posted = [c for c in comments if c['issue_url'].endswith(f'/issues/{fork_pr}')]
        folder = out/str(upstream)
        folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        if run:
            subprocess.run(['gh', 'run', 'download', '-R', a.fork, str(run['id']), '-n', 'amu-report', '-D', str(folder)],
                           capture_output=True)
        body = posted[-1]['body'] if posted else ''
        (folder/'comment.md').write_text(body)
        row = dict(upstream=upstream, fork_pr=fork_pr, run=run['id'] if run else None,
                   amu_job_s=(when(amu['completed_at']) - when(amu['started_at'])).seconds if amu else None,
                   queue_s=(when(amu['started_at']) - when(created)).seconds if amu else None,
                   opened_to_comment_s=(when(posted[-1]['created_at']) - when(created)).seconds if posted else None,
                   posted=bool(posted), first=body.splitlines()[0] if body else None)
        table.append(row)
        print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
    (out/'live.json').write_text(json.dumps(table, indent=1))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

records (#88), and the first line from per-hunk evidence states (#89). The Action was pinned to v0.6.0 on
abslock128w/attrs. The same 15 heads were opened as fork pull requests #16–#30 against new base branches (`amu6-base-*`:
the merge base plus the v0.6.0 workflows). Python 3.12, as before. Files are in `v060/`: `data.json`, `labels.json`,
`comments/` and `reports.tar.xz`.

### Losses first

- **Two first lines are wrong (13 of 15 right), and both are noise.** One defect behind both: how a changed line
  without bytecode was mapped. #91 fixes it on main, after v0.6.0, so these comments still show it.
  - attrs 1606: the changed `add_replace` runs only on Python 3.13+, yet the line says "every changed hunk ran on both
    sides (at import)". The added comment stood for the whole function, whose `def` line runs at import.
  - attrs 1454: "`src/attr/_make.py:1436` ran in no test". The hunk is a `nonlocal hash` line in a function nearly
    every test runs. `nonlocal` has no bytecode, and its hunk was watched through no line at all.
- **attrs 1592 leads with type-check examples.** Its first line lists 3 hunks in `typing-examples/` that ran in no
  test. That is true, but it comes before the 8 evidence tests a reviewer would want first.
- **One non-test counted as a test.** On 1469, `tests/typing_example.py::test` was a candidate. It is a mypy example
  pytest never collects, so it is reported as unrunnable.
- **The job is slower when the change is small.** The whole suite runs on both sides, so the job took 52–125 s, against
  34–132 s at v0.5.1.

|---|---:|---:|

| First line correct | 11 | 13 |
| Adds something | 2 | 5 |
| Adds noise | 2 | 2 |
| False behaviour rows | 62 (attrs 1509) | 0 |
| Real behaviour rows | 0 | 0 (on Python 3.12; see below) |
| Suite run, AMU's test functions | 1 % to 70 % | 100 % (all runnable tests, every PR) |
| Tests that would catch a raise, missed | 8 of 8 on attrs 1636 | 0 of 1,197 across the 15 |
| AMU job | 34–132 s | 52–125 s |
| Pull request opened → comment | 62–157 s | 82–150 s |

- **Suite covered.** Each run measured the whole suite on the merge base inside its budget, then ran it whole on the
  head: 632 to 667 test functions. "Suite run" for v0.5.1 is its candidates over the same count.
- **Tests that would catch a raise.** For each pull request, the first changed statement of each hunk on the head was
  made to raise, only while a test runs (`evaluation/generalize/raise_missed.py`). The whole suite then ran, and a
  test failing with the marker counts as a catcher. The catchers were measured locally on Python 3.14, against each
  live comment's candidates.
- **Behaviour rows.**
  - attrs 1509 went from 62 false rows to 0, with no set-aside rule. Each `Attribute` object is recorded on the side
    that built it, so the two inputs differ (one has the new slot) and are not compared.
  - On Python 3.12 no row appeared: the add_replace change behind attrs 1606 and 1507 runs only on 3.13+. Run locally
    on 3.14, paired records show it on both (the class dictionary holds `evolve` itself before 1606 and a local proxy
    after), and those rows are real.

### Per pull request

{table}
- **Labels:** `v060/labels.json`, same rubric as the v0.5.1 labels above.
- **"Adds something" on 1600 and 1507:** the comment names a hunk that cannot run on this job's Python. On 1507 that
  hunk is the change that started mutating `evolve`'s dunders.
'''
p='evaluation/pilot/attrs/REPORT.md'
s=open(p).read().rstrip('\n')+section
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

- **Static gaps shown even after the whole suite ran.**
  - On all 15 comments a gap says "2,3xx call sites unresolved repo-wide". On httpx 3401 another says "No existing
    test reaches the change within five source hops".
  - Both are static-graph statements. These runs selected nothing statically: the whole suite ran on both sides, and
    the hunks are recorded as run. On 3401 the gap contradicts the hunk list (defect 1).
- **A hang in the measurement, not in AMU.**
  - The raise measure's first try hung on httpx 3699: a raise inside the test server's code left a client waiting.
  - It was rerun with a 60 s per-test timeout. A test that times out that way does not count as a catcher, so the
    catcher counts are a lower bound.
- **The job is slower than a selective one would be.** The whole suite of about 540 test functions runs on both sides,
  so the AMU job took 50–109 s. That is still small next to httpx's own CI.
- **Adds something on 3 of 15 only.** For most of these pull requests the comment confirms, as a green CI run would,
  that every changed hunk ran and nothing flipped.

## Results

{table}
| | httpx (15) |
|---|---:|
| Comment posted | 15 of 15 |
| First line correct | 15 |
| Adds something a reviewer would want | 3 (3571, 3412, 3394) |

| Adds noise | 0 |

  the default.

  Test Suite and Publish were disabled on the fork, so only AMU's workflows ran.

    v0.6.0 workflows.
  - Its head is `amu-pr-<n>`, the upstream pull request's own head.

    then ran locally on Python 3.14, and a test failing with the marker counts as a catcher
    (`evaluation/generalize/raise_missed.py`).
  - This was compared with each live comment's candidates. Every candidate set was the whole suite, so 0 missed
    follows from it, and the measure confirms it.

     the static graph, which this run did not use to select.
   - **Expected:** when the selection mode is the whole suite, or every hunk has a recorded state, these gaps should not
     be shown.
   - **Reproduction:** `3401/report.json` in `reports.tar.xz`, keys `gaps` and `hunks`.
2. **"at import" for hunks in function signatures.**
   - **What happened:** on 3419 and 3394, hunks that remove a parameter from a function's signature read "ran on both
     sides (at import)". A signature line runs when the module defines the function, but the change matters at every
     call, and the comment does not say whether a test called the function.
   - **Reproduction:** `3419/report.json`, the hunks at `httpx/_api.py` with `why: at import`.

   - **What happened:** changing a type annotation is reported by where it runs, never as no code change. On these 15
     every such hunk sat beside a code change, so no first line was wrong, but an annotation-only change would read
     "ran on both sides" rather than "docstring or comment changes only".
   - **Reproduction:** `3380/report.json`, the hunks in `httpx/_types.py`.

## Verdict

**v0.6.0 held on an untuned repository.**
- 15 of 15 comments posted, and 15 of 15 first lines were right.
- 0 false behaviour rows and 0 noise.
- Every pull request ran the whole suite, and no test that would catch a raise of the changed code was missed.

That is the opposite of the attrs pilot at v0.5.1, where 4 first lines were wrong, 62 rows were false and the

**Losses so far:**
- **Large suites fall back to the static graph.** On Django and sympy the suite doesn't fit the 300 s budget, so the merge-base recording covers only part of it and every hunk falls back to static selection. That is where Django 22154 missed 11 of the 69 tests that would catch a raise.
- **Fixing it needs a whole-suite recording per merge base, made outside the PR job.** One 20-minute job can't record suites this size. A smaller fix: hits from a partial recording are currently thrown away and should count as candidates.
- **Two wrong first lines on attrs at v0.6.0.** In 1606, code that only runs on Python 3.13+ read "ran on both sides"; in 1454, a `nonlocal` line read "ran in no test". - **Real rows lost.** On Flask 5812 most of the old real rows came back, but some cases where only an argument's state changed are now dropped. Rows compare only the return value or exception, as you defined them.

**httpx defects, recorded and not fixed:**
1. Static-graph gaps still show after a whole-suite run ("call sites unresolved"; on 3401, "no existing test reaches the change", next to hunks recorded as run).
2. Hunks that change a function signature read "(at import)" and don't say whether any test called the function.
3. Type-annotation lines count as code, so an annotation-only change would read "ran on both sides" rather than "docstring or comment changes only".

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.

6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.

"""Collect a fork pilot's live results: per pull request the AMU job time, open-to-comment time, the comment, and the
artifact (report.json, meta.json, patch.diff). Usage: python collect.py --fork owner/name --opened FILE --out DIR
FILE rows: fork PR number, upstream number, created_at (as printed by replay.py)."""
import argparse
import datetime as D
import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path


def api(path):
    return json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['gh', 'api', path]))


def when(text):
    return D.datetime.fromisoformat(text.replace('Z', '+00:00'))


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument('--fork', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--opened', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--out', required=True)
    a = p.parse_args()
    out = Path(a.out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rows = []
    for line in Path(a.opened).read_text().splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) < 3 or not parts[0].isdigit():
            continue
        first, second, created = int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]), parts[2]
        rows.append((min(first, second), max(first, second), created))  # the fork's numbers are the small ones
    runs = api(f'repos/{a.fork}/actions/runs?per_page=100&event=pull_request')['workflow_runs']
    comments = []
    page = 1
    while True:
        got = api(f'repos/{a.fork}/issues/comments?per_page=100&page={page}')
        comments += got
        if len(got) < 100:
            break
        page += 1
    table = []
    for fork_pr, upstream, created in rows:
        pr = api(f'repos/{a.fork}/pulls/{fork_pr}')
        mine = [r for r in runs if r['name'] == 'AMU pull request' and r['head_sha'] == pr['head']['sha']
                and any(x['number'] == fork_pr for x in r.get('pull_requests') or [])] or \
               [r for r in runs if r['name'] == 'AMU pull request' and r['head_sha'] == pr['head']['sha'] and r['created_at'] >= created]
        run = sorted(mine, key=lambda r: r['created_at'])[-1] if mine else None
        jobs = api(f"repos/{a.fork}/actions/runs/{run['id']}/jobs")['jobs'] if run else []
        amu = next((j for j in jobs if j['name'] == 'amu' and j.get('completed_at')), None)
        posted = [c for c in comments if c['issue_url'].endswith(f'/issues/{fork_pr}')]
        folder = out/str(upstream)
        folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        if run:
            subprocess.run(['gh', 'run', 'download', '-R', a.fork, str(run['id']), '-n', 'amu-report', '-D', str(folder)],
                           capture_output=True)
        body = posted[-1]['body'] if posted else ''
        (folder/'comment.md').write_text(body)
        row = dict(upstream=upstream, fork_pr=fork_pr, run=run['id'] if run else None,
                   amu_job_s=(when(amu['completed_at']) - when(amu['started_at'])).seconds if amu else None,
                   queue_s=(when(amu['started_at']) - when(created)).seconds if amu else None,
                   opened_to_comment_s=(when(posted[-1]['created_at']) - when(created)).seconds if posted else None,
                   posted=bool(posted), first=body.splitlines()[0] if body else None)
        table.append(row)
        print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
    (out/'live.json').write_text(json.dumps(table, indent=1))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
