tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. ## Follow-up: the three leftovers fixed (#77–#79), 2026-11-02

Each leftover defect above got its own PR with a test that fails on the code before it. The three pull requests they affect (Flask #5812, Django #22026, Django #22176) were re-run on all three together (engine `0b8312b`, `main` plus #78 and #79). The other 44 cannot change: none of them had a false row or a side-by-side start failure. `labels.json` holds the updated labels; the comments and reports are in `leftovers/`.

| Fix | PR | What it changes |
|---|---|---|
| Attributes new per class | #77 | Constructor attributes count as new per class (and its subclasses in the same file), not per file. |
| Uncopyable arguments put back | #78 | Arguments that copy neither way get their attributes put back after each run. As-changed failures inside a method of an object the old code built are set aside. |
| Command line too long | #79 | Labels run in halves when the command line exceeds the system limit. There is no "none … was called" gap when the runner never started. |

The `RuntimeError` rows on Flask #5812 were not what this report said above. They were not context state the old code set up. Tracing the run showed that `AppContext(app)` cannot be copied (the app holds a lock), so side-by-side ran the as-changed `AppContext.__init__` on the live context being built. That left `_request = None` and the other new attributes on it, and the test went on to push that half-rebuilt context. Every later as-changed function that read it failed. #78 puts such arguments back after each run.

| | Before #77–#79 | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Flask #5812 rows | 35 (14 real, 21 false) | 17 (16 real, 1 false) |
| Flask #5812 calls set aside as built before the change | 66 | 91 |
| Django #22026 side-by-side | did not start | 71 calls of 2 functions compared, 0 rows |
| Django #22176 side-by-side | did not start | 28 calls of 2 functions compared, 0 rows |
| All 47: behaviour rows | 52 (31 real, 21 false) | 34 (33 real, 1 false) |
| All 47: adds noise | 3 | 2 (Django #22176 subTest evidence, sympy #29693 adds-only) |
| All 47: first line correct | 40 | 40 |

Django #22026 now also shows #71 on real code. `get_prefetcher` was compared on captured calls, and the 9 `NameError` rows of v0.4.2 do not come back.

What is still false:
- **Flask #5812, 1 row:** `make_default_options_response` raises `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'allowed_methods'`. The old context has no matched URL rule where the new code looks for one.
- **Two noise PRs:** Django #22176 (subTest failure blocks not parsed) and sympy #29693 ("adds new code only" for a method found by name dispatch). Both are outside these fixes.

## Follow-up: docstring-only first line, 2026-11-02

The first line was wrong on 7 of 47 after v0.5.0. Two of them, Django #22046 and sympy #30838, change only a docstring, and they read "no flip … whether any ran the changed code was not seen". The comment now says **"AMU: docstring or comment changes only"** in that case: every changed production function differs only in its docstring, comments or layout (side-by-side's own finding), and nothing else in those files changed. Re-rendering all 47 stored reports changes the first line of exactly these two. First line correct: 40 → 42 of 47.

## Follow-up: the three leftovers fixed (#77–#79), 2026-11-02

Each leftover defect above got its own PR with a test that fails on the code before it. The three pull requests they affect (Flask #5812, Django #22026, Django #22176) were re-run on all three together (engine `0b8312b`, `main` plus #78 and #79). The other 44 cannot change: none of them had a false row or a side-by-side start failure. `labels.json` holds the updated labels; the comments and reports are in `leftovers/`.

| Fix | PR | What it changes |
|---|---|---|
| Attributes new per class | #77 | Constructor attributes count as new per class (and its subclasses in the same file), not per file. |
| Uncopyable arguments put back | #78 | Arguments that copy neither way get their attributes put back after each run. As-changed failures inside a method of an object the old code built are set aside. |
| Command line too long | #79 | Labels run in halves when the command line exceeds the system limit. There is no "none … was called" gap when the runner never started. |

The `RuntimeError` rows on Flask #5812 were not what this report said above. They were not context state the old code set up. Tracing the run showed that `AppContext(app)` cannot be copied (the app holds a lock), so side-by-side ran the as-changed `AppContext.__init__` on the live context being built. That left `_request = None` and the other new attributes on it, and the test went on to push that half-rebuilt context. Every later as-changed function that read it failed. #78 puts such arguments back after each run.

| | Before #77–#79 | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Flask #5812 rows | 35 (14 real, 21 false) | 17 (16 real, 1 false) |
| Flask #5812 calls set aside as built before the change | 66 | 91 |
| Django #22026 side-by-side | did not start | 71 calls of 2 functions compared, 0 rows |
| Django #22176 side-by-side | did not start | 28 calls of 2 functions compared, 0 rows |
| All 47: behaviour rows | 52 (31 real, 21 false) | 34 (33 real, 1 false) |
| All 47: adds noise | 3 | 2 (Django #22176 subTest evidence, sympy #29693 adds-only) |
| All 47: first line correct | 40 | 40 |

Django #22026 now also shows #71 on real code. `get_prefetcher` was compared on captured calls, and the 9 `NameError` rows of v0.4.2 do not come back.

What is still false:
- **Flask #5812, 1 row:** `make_default_options_response` raises `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'allowed_methods'`. The old context has no matched URL rule where the new code looks for one.
- **Two noise PRs:** Django #22176 (subTest failure blocks not parsed) and sympy #29693 ("adds new code only" for a method found by name dispatch). Both are outside these fixes.

## Follow-up: docstring-only first line, 2026-11-02

The first line was wrong on 7 of 47 after v0.5.0. Two of them, Django #22046 and sympy #30838, change only a docstring, and they read "no flip … whether any ran the changed code was not seen". The comment now says **"AMU: docstring or comment changes only"** in that case: every changed production function differs only in its docstring, comments or layout (side-by-side's own finding), and nothing else in those files changed. Re-rendering all 47 stored reports changes the first line of exactly these two. First line correct: 40 → 42 of 47.

# The three causes, measured on the 47 set (2026-11-03)

The 47 set was re-run locally on engine `43d8b82`, the code released as v0.6.0. It is the same 47 pull requests from
Django (17), sympy (20) and Flask (10) as `evaluation/performance-v042` and `evaluation/performance-fixes`: Python 3.14, a
300 s budget per side and a 1,200 s wall cap. Each pull request also got the raise measure (`raise_missed.py`). A
`raise` is injected into a changed function and fires only inside a running test. The tests that fail with it are the
tests that would catch a raise; "missed" counts those that AMU did not run. The live pilots on attrs and httpx are in
`evaluation/pilot/attrs/REPORT.md` and `evaluation/pilot/httpx/REPORT.md`.

Files: `v060-47/labels.json` (hand labels, with the prior label beside each), `v060-47/data.json` (per pull request:
mode, candidate sources, rows, raise catchers and misses, first line, seconds), `v060-47/comments/`, and
`v060-47/reports.tar.xz` (report, raise and meta files).

## Losses

- **41 false behaviour rows on three pull requests. The goal was 0.** They come from three causes, and none is a
  per-repo rule:
  - **A version string read from each side's checkout.** On Django 22026 (7 rows) and 22171 (3 rows), a model

content.text:
All three runs are finished. The causes didn't fully hold: the 47 set has 41 false behaviour rows (the target was 0), and 3 first lines regressed. The 47-set report is merged as [#93](https://github.com/abslock128w/AMU/pull/93), losses first.

**Numbers**
- **47 set (v0.6.0, run locally):** first line right on 43 of 47, up from 42. 4 fixed, 3 regressed (Django 22026, Django 22171, sympy 30781): each now announces behaviour differences that are false. Behaviour rows: 384 real, 41 false. 24 of the 33 real rows from before are still found. Whole suite run on 10 of 47 (all of Flask).
- **attrs, v0.5.1 → v0.6.0 (live):** first line right 11 → 13 of 15, useful 2 → 5, false rows 62 → 0, share of the suite run 1–99 % → 100 %.
- **httpx (v0.6.0, live, never tuned on):** 15 of 15 posted and right, 3 useful, 0 noise, whole suite every time. Job 50–109 s; PR opened to comment 77–155 s.

**Tests that would catch a raise, missed / false rows**

| Repo | Missed | False rows |
|---|---|---|
| attrs | 0 of 1,197 (1636 alone was 8 of 8 before) | 0 |
| httpx | 0 of 933 | 0 (1 real) |
| Flask | 0 of 1,490 | 0 (344 real) |
| Django | 61 of 495 | 11 |
| sympy | 11 of 11,237 | 30 |

- **Where the misses come from:** Django and sympy suites never fit the 300 s budget, so the merge-base recording is cut off and selection falls back to the static graph on every PR. The misses are on Django 22046 (41, a docstring-only change), 22154 (11) and 22095 (9), and sympy 30808 (11).
- **Where the false rows come from:**
  - A version string computed from each side's checkout ('6.2' on one side, '6.2.dev…' on the other).
  - Each side's folder path stored split into parts, which the path cleanup misses.
  - A lazily filled hash cache (`_mhash`) on sympy 30781, where the results are otherwise identical.
- **Real rows lost:** the same hash cache changes with each process's hash seed, so real differences don't repeat on a rerun and get dropped. That is why all 9 lost real rows are on sympy (30803: 3, 30741: 6).

**httpx defects (recorded, not fixed)**
1. The static graph's gap notes still appear after a whole-suite run (on 3401, "no existing test reaches the change" next to hunks that ran).
2. Hunks that change a function signature read "(at import)" and don't say whether any test called the function (3419, 3394).
3. Type-annotation lines count as code, so an annotation-only change reads as code that ran.

**Unfinished, and why**
- **The false-row and lost-row causes above are not fixed.** I found them at the end of the run, and engine changes were frozen during it. The fix is to stop comparing values that come from each side's own checkout or process: version strings, folder paths split into parts, and hash values. A new PR series with tests is needed.
- **Large suites need a whole-suite recording per merge base, made outside the PR job.** One 20-minute job can't record Django or sympy. A smaller step: tests a cut-off recording saw running a hunk should still count as candidates.
- **Two first lines are still off.**
  - Django 22158 adds code for Python 3.15 only, and still reads as run.
  - Django 22186 reads "ran on both sides" although its Windows-only line ran in no test. Its label stays "right", as before.
- **sympy 30780 has no raise measure.** Two run streams collided in one work folder.
- **The 47-set workspace had been deleted.** I rebuilt it in `~/Documents/ChatGPT/AMU/generalize-2026-11-02`; there is no older-engine raise measure on the 47 set to compare against.
- **v0.6.0 is a GitHub release only, not on PyPI.** The Action installs from the tag. #91, which fixed the two wrong attrs first lines, is on main but not in a release.

httpx held at 15/15 untuned, so the three causes were right. Two remain, both design, fix them generally; no rule may name a specific value kind (version string, path, hash).

Cause 4, large suites: when the suite does not fit the budget, selection falls back to the static graph and misses tests (Django 61 of 495, sympy 11 of 11,237). Fix: whole-suite recording happens outside the PR job. Add a third workflow to INSTALL-NOTE, scheduled (nightly and on push to the default branch), that records per-test coverage for the whole suite at that commit with the sys.monitoring tracer, splits across a job matrix if needed, and stores it keyed by commit (actions/cache or a release asset, your call; document size and retention). The PR job loads the nearest ancestor recording of the merge base, applies the diff since that commit (tests touching changed files since then are added as candidates), and never records. If no recording exists it does what it does today and the first line says "no suite recording for base; selected statically". Also: tests a cut-off recording did see running a hunk count as candidates. Measure on Django and sympy: missed raise catchers must be 0.

Cause 5, process-dependent values: false rows come from values that belong to the process or checkout, not the behaviour. Fix generally: run the base side's paired recording twice (second run can be the subset of tests that produced rows); any record field that differs base-vs-base is nondeterministic and is excluded from the base-vs-head comparison for that function. Report the excluded field count. The lost real rows on sympy (hash seed) should return where the result itself is stable. Measure on the 47 set: false rows 0, and real rows retained vs the 33 at v0.5.1 and the 384 now.

Also fix the three httpx defects and the two Django first lines (22158 Python 3.15 gate, 22186 Windows-only line) under cause 3's state model, and the version-gate detection must cover sys.platform as well as sys.version_info.

Then release v0.7.0 (GitHub and PyPI), re-run the 47 set locally and the attrs and httpx forks live, and run a seventh untuned repo: fork pallets/jinja to abslock128w/jinja (test execution approved), same protocol. Reports as before. Final message: numbers per repo (first line, useful, noise, false rows, missed catchers, suite share), then losses, then unfinished.

1	"""Execution-first selection: which tests run on each side of a change, chosen from what the tests were seen to run.
2	
3	The order of evidence:
4	
5	1. **The whole suite.** When the suite's last measured time on the code before the change fits the budget, or no
6	   time was measured yet, every test runs on that side, recorded (record module). If that run finishes inside the
7	   planned share of the budget, every test also runs on the code after the change: no selection.
8	2. **Coverage of the changed code.** Otherwise the candidates are the tests the recording saw entering the code each
9	   hunk changes (hunks module): this run's recording, or one kept for the same commit (``Coverage``).
10	3. **The static graph**, only for a hunk no recording can speak for: code the change adds where nothing ran before, a
11	   hunk whose file was not recorded, a module-level hunk that runs at import, or a recording that did not finish.
12	
13	Every candidate keeps where it came from (``sources``), and each hunk the tests that ran it on each side.
14	"""
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import hashlib
18	import json
19	import time
20	from pathlib import Path
21	
22	from . import hunks as hunk_split
23	from . import record, replay
24	
25	FILL = 0.8  # share of the budget a whole-suite run may take and still be run on the other side too
26	WHOLE = 400  # tests per process in one chunk of a whole-suite run: fewer runner starts; a chunk the budget stops is lost
27	ALL, COVERAGE, STATIC, OWN = 'all of the suite', 'coverage', 'static graph', "the change's own test"
28	
29	
30	def _sha(text):
31	    return hashlib.sha256((text or '').encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
32	
33	
34	class Coverage:
35	    """Per-test coverage of changed files on one commit, kept between runs (the CI cache is keyed by the merge base).
36	    For each file: the hash of its text, the lines that were watched, and {line: [test]}. Only a recording of the whole
37	    suite is kept, so a watched line nobody ran was run by no test."""
38	
39	    def __init__(self, folder, key):
40	        self.path = Path(folder)/'coverage'/f'{key}.json' if folder and key else None
41	        try:
42	            self.data = json.loads(self.path.read_text()) if self.path else {}
43	        except (OSError, ValueError):
44	            self.data = {}
45	
46	    def tests(self, path, text, lines):
47	        """Tests that ran any of ``lines``, or None when this commit's recording did not watch all of them."""
48	        entry = (self.data.get('files') or {}).get(path)
49	        if not entry or entry.get('sha') != _sha(text) or not set(lines) <= set(entry.get('watched', [])):
50	            return None
51	        hits = entry.get('hits', {})
52	        return {test for line in lines for test in hits.get(str(line), [])}
53	
54	    def store(self, before_src, watched, coverage, tests_run):
55	        if not self.path:
56	            return
57	        files = dict(self.data.get('files') or {})
58	        for path, lines in watched.items():
59	            hits = {}
60	            for test, seen in coverage.items():
61	                for line in seen.get(path, ()):
62	                    hits.setdefault(str(line), []).append(test)
63	            files[path] = dict(sha=_sha(before_src.get(path)), watched=sorted(lines), hits={k: sorted(v) for k, v in hits.items()})
64	        try:
65	            self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
66	            self.path.write_text(json.dumps(dict(files=files, tests=tests_run)))
67	        except OSError:
68	            pass

71	def _chunks(execute, runner, python, tree, ids, scratch, name, budget, deadline, parts, env, chunk):
72	    """Run ``ids`` in order, a chunk at a time, until they are done or ``budget`` seconds are used. Returns
73	    ({id: state}, [problems], seconds, {id: the slice it ran in}); ``problems`` holds 'wall cap' when the deadline
74	    stopped it."""
75	    found, problems, context, began = {}, [], {}, time.perf_counter()
76	    for start in range(0, len(ids), chunk * parts):
77	        left = budget - (time.perf_counter() - began)
78	        if deadline is not None:
79	            if deadline - time.monotonic() <= 1:
80	                problems.append('wall cap')
81	                break
82	            left = min(left, deadline - time.monotonic())
83	        if left <= 1:
84	            break
85	        part = ids[start:start + chunk * parts]
86	        got, said = execute(runner, python, tree, part, scratch, f'{name}-{start}', left, parts, env)
87	        found.update(got)
88	        for slice_ in [part[i::parts] for i in range(parts)] if parts > 1 else [part]:
89	            context.update({ident: slice_ for ident in slice_})
90	        problems += [p for p in said if p not in problems]
91	        if 'timed out' in said:
92	            if deadline is not None and deadline - time.monotonic() <= 1:
93	                problems.append('wall cap')
94	            break
95	    return found, problems, round(time.perf_counter() - began, 1), context
96	
97	
98	RERUN = 60  # seconds at most for running again, on each side, the tests whose calls differed
99	
100	
101	def compare(execute, runner, python, trees, plan, scratch, deadline, parts, chunk, calls_b, calls_a, both, base_watch,
102	            head_watch, moved=None):
103	    """Calls of each changed function present on both sides, paired by test and call index (record.pair). A pair whose
104	    outputs differ on equal inputs is kept only if a second run of its test, on each side, gives the same two outputs:
105	    a difference neither side repeats is nondeterminism, counted and not shown."""
106	    rows, counts = record.pair([c for c in calls_b if c['function'] in both], [c for c in calls_a if c['function'] in both], moved)
107	    tests = sorted({row['test'] for row in rows})  # one representative test per distinct row
108	    kept, unstable = rows, 0
109	    if tests:
110	        again = {}
111	        for side, watch, targets in (('before', base_watch, plan['targets_before']), ('after', head_watch, plan['targets_after'])):
112	            folder = Path(scratch)/f'record-{side}-again'
113	            env = record.prepare(folder, trees[side], watch, targets)
114	            _chunks(execute, runner, python, trees[side], tests, scratch, f'{side}-again', RERUN, deadline, parts, env, chunk)
115	            again[side] = {(c['test'], c['function'], c['n']): c.get('result') or c['output'] for c in record.read(folder, trees[side],
116	                                                                                                runner.cwd(trees[side]))[1]}
117	        kept = [row for row in rows if again['before'].get((row['test'], row['function'], row['n'])) == row['digest'][0]
118	                and again['after'].get((row['test'], row['function'], row['n'])) == row['digest'][1]]
119	        unstable = len(rows) - len(kept)
120	    called = sorted({c['function'] for c in calls_b if c['function'] in both} | {c['function'] for c in calls_a if c['function'] in both})
121	    return dict(rows=kept, counts=dict(counts, unstable=unstable), called=called, compared_functions=len(both))
122	
123	
124	def plan_hunks(edits, before_src, after_src):
125	    """Every hunk of the changed production files (tests are the change's own tests, replayed apart)."""
126	    return [h for path, edit in edits.items() if path.endswith('.py') and not replay.is_test_file(path)
127	            for h in hunk_split.split(path, edit, before_src.get(path) or '', after_src.get(path) or '')]
128	
129	
130	def run(execute, runner, python, trees, edits, before_src, after_src, plan, scratch, budget, deadline, parts, chunk,
131	        remembered, cache_folder):
132	    """Both sides of the change, chosen and run as the module says. Returns a dict: ids (the candidates run on the code
133	    after the change, in order), before/after ({id: state}), context, sources ({id: where it came from}), mode, hunks
134	    (each with the tests that ran it on each side), recorded coverage and calls per side, seconds, problems."""
135	    hunks = plan_hunks(edits, before_src, after_src)
136	    base_watch, head_watch = {}, {}
137	    for h in hunks:
138	        base_watch.setdefault(h['path'], set()).update(h['base'])
139	        head_watch.setdefault(h['path'], set()).update(h['head'])
140	    # Every function a hunk changes, on each side where it exists, is recorded in that side's own run (record).
141	    moved = {}
142	    for h in hunks:
143	        for qual in set(h['old_touched']) & set(h['new_touched']):
144	            found = hunk_split.changed_defaults(before_src.get(h['path']) or '', after_src.get(h['path']) or '', qual)
145	            if found:
146	                moved[f"{h['path']}#{qual}"] = found
147	    targets_before = sorted({(h['path'], qual, tuple(sorted(moved.get(f"{h['path']}#{qual}", {}))))
148	                             for h in hunks for qual in h['old_touched']})
149	    targets_after = sorted({(h['path'], qual, tuple(sorted(moved.get(f"{h['path']}#{qual}", {}))))
150	                            for h in hunks for qual in h['new_touched']})
151	    plan = dict(plan, targets_before=targets_before, targets_after=targets_after)
152	    own = list(dict.fromkeys(plan.get('own') or []))
153	    mine = set(own)
154	    static = [i for i in plan.get('static') or [] if i not in mine]
155	    everything = [i for i in plan.get('everything') or [] if i not in mine]
156	    durations = remembered.get('durations') or {}
157	    kept = Coverage(cache_folder, plan.get('key'))
158	    suite = remembered.get('suite_seconds')
159	    fits = suite is None or suite <= budget * FILL
160	    # What a kept recording of this commit already says about each hunk; None where it cannot speak.
161	    known = {(h['path'], h['index']): kept.tests(h['path'], before_src.get(h['path']), h['base']) if h['base'] else None
162	             for h in hunks}
163	    # A recording runs unless the suite is known not to fit and this commit's kept recording speaks for every hunk with
164	    # code before the change.
165	    exploring = fits or any(h['base'] and known[h['path'], h['index']] is None for h in hunks)
166	    if exploring:
167	        # Static candidates first, so a run the budget stops still has their outcomes; then the rest, quickest first.
168	        first = set(static)
169	        rest = sorted((i for i in everything if i not in first), key=lambda i: (durations.get(i, 0.5), i))
170	        base_ids = list(dict.fromkeys([*static, *rest]))
171	    else:
172	        base_ids = None  # chosen from the kept recording below, then run
173	    sources, gaps = {}, []
174	    before_dir = Path(scratch)/'record-before'
175	    env = record.prepare(before_dir, trees['before'], base_watch, plan.get('targets_before') or [])
176	    coverage_b, calls_b = {}, []
177	    if base_ids is not None:
178	        found_b, problems_b, seconds_b, _ = _chunks(execute, runner, python, trees['before'], base_ids, scratch, 'before',
179	                                                   budget, deadline, parts, env, WHOLE if fits else chunk)
180	        coverage_b, calls_b, skipped_b = record.read(before_dir, trees['before'], runner.cwd(trees['before']))
181	        complete = bool(base_ids) and all(i in found_b for i in base_ids) and any(
182	            state in ('passed', 'failed', 'skipped') for state in found_b.values())
183	    else:
184	        found_b, problems_b, seconds_b, complete, skipped_b = {}, [], 0.0, False, {}
185	    mode = ALL if exploring and complete and seconds_b <= budget * FILL else COVERAGE
186	    if exploring and complete:
187	        remembered['suite_seconds'] = seconds_b
188	        kept.store(before_src, {p: v for p, v in base_watch.items() if v}, coverage_b, len(base_ids))
189	    elif exploring and not complete and fits:
190	        # The whole suite did not fit: next time the kept recording, or the static graph, chooses.
191	        remembered['suite_seconds'] = max(seconds_b, budget)
192	    for h in hunks:
193	        key = (h['path'], h['index'])
194	        if complete or not exploring:
195	            ran = record.tests_on(coverage_b, h['path'], h['base']) if exploring else known.get(key)
196	        else:
197	            ran = None
198	        h['base_tests'] = sorted(t for t in (ran or ()) if t != record.IMPORT) if ran is not None else None
199	        h['at_import'] = bool(ran and record.IMPORT in ran)
200	    if mode == ALL:
201	        head_ids = [*own, *base_ids]
202	        sources.update({i: ALL for i in base_ids})
203	    else:
204	        chosen = []
205	        for h in hunks:
206	            if h['base_tests'] is not None and not (h['at_import'] and not h['base_tests']):
207	                chosen += [t for t in h['base_tests'] if t not in mine]
208	                sources.update({t: COVERAGE for t in h['base_tests'] if t not in mine and t not in sources})
209	        if any(h['base_tests'] is None or (h['at_import'] and not h['base_tests']) for h in hunks) or not hunks:
210	            chosen += static
211	            for t in static:
212	                sources.setdefault(t, STATIC)
213	        head_ids = list(dict.fromkeys([*own, *chosen]))
214	    sources.update({i: OWN for i in own})
215	    after_dir = Path(scratch)/'record-after'
216	    env = record.prepare(after_dir, trees['after'], head_watch, plan.get('targets_after') or [])
217	    found_a, problems_a, seconds_a, context = _chunks(execute, runner, python, trees['after'], head_ids, scratch, 'after',
218	                                                      budget, deadline, parts, env, WHOLE if mode == ALL else chunk)
219	    coverage_a, calls_a, skipped_a = record.read(after_dir, trees['after'], runner.cwd(trees['after']))
220	    # Candidates the code before the change has not run yet (chosen from a kept recording, or from the static graph):
221	    # run there too, so each outcome on the changed code has its partner.
222	    missing = [i for i in head_ids if i not in mine and i in found_a and i not in found_b]
223	    if missing:
224	        env = record.prepare(Path(scratch)/'record-before-2', trees['before'], base_watch, plan.get('targets_before') or [])
225	        more, said, took, _ = _chunks(execute, runner, python, trees['before'], missing, scratch, 'before-2',

227	        found_b.update(more)
228	        problems_b += [p for p in said if p not in problems_b]
229	        seconds_b += took

235	    for h in hunks:

237	        h['head_at_import'] = record.IMPORT in record.tests_on(coverage_a, h['path'], h['head'])

248	    if exploring and not complete and not cut:

import json
import time
from pathlib import Path

    """Per-test coverage of changed files on one commit, kept between runs (the CI cache is keyed by the merge base).
    For each file: the hash of its text, the lines that were watched, and {line: [test]}. Only a recording of the whole
    suite is kept, so a watched line nobody ran was run by no test."""

        self.path = Path(folder)/'coverage'/f'{key}.json' if folder and key else None

        except (OSError, ValueError):

    def tests(self, path, text, lines):
        """Tests that ran any of ``lines``, or None when this commit's recording did not watch all of them."""
        entry = (self.data.get('files') or {}).get(path)
        if not entry or entry.get('sha') != _sha(text) or not set(lines) <= set(entry.get('watched', [])):
            return None
        hits = entry.get('hits', {})
        return {test for line in lines for test in hits.get(str(line), [])}

    def store(self, before_src, watched, coverage, tests_run):
        if not self.path:
            return
        files = dict(self.data.get('files') or {})
        for path, lines in watched.items():
            hits = {}
            for test, seen in coverage.items():
                for line in seen.get(path, ()):
                    hits.setdefault(str(line), []).append(test)
            files[path] = dict(sha=_sha(before_src.get(path)), watched=sorted(lines), hits={k: sorted(v) for k, v in hits.items()})
        try:
            self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            self.path.write_text(json.dumps(dict(files=files, tests=tests_run)))
        except OSError:
            pass


def _chunks(execute, runner, python, tree, ids, scratch, name, budget, deadline, parts, env, chunk):
    """Run ``ids`` in order, a chunk at a time, until they are done or ``budget`` seconds are used. Returns
    ({id: state}, [problems], seconds, {id: the slice it ran in}); ``problems`` holds 'wall cap' when the deadline
    stopped it."""
    found, problems, context, began = {}, [], {}, time.perf_counter()
    for start in range(0, len(ids), chunk * parts):
        left = budget - (time.perf_counter() - began)
        if deadline is not None:
            if deadline - time.monotonic() <= 1:
                problems.append('wall cap')
                break
            left = min(left, deadline - time.monotonic())
        if left <= 1:
            break
        part = ids[start:start + chunk * parts]
        got, said = execute(runner, python, tree, part, scratch, f'{name}-{start}', left, parts, env)
        found.update(got)
        for slice_ in [part[i::parts] for i in range(parts)] if parts > 1 else [part]:
            context.update({ident: slice_ for ident in slice_})
        problems += [p for p in said if p not in problems]
        if 'timed out' in said:
            if deadline is not None and deadline - time.monotonic() <= 1:
                problems.append('wall cap')
            break
    return found, problems, round(time.perf_counter() - began, 1), context


RERUN = 60  # seconds at most for running again, on each side, the tests whose calls differed


def compare(execute, runner, python, trees, plan, scratch, deadline, parts, chunk, calls_b, calls_a, both, base_watch,
            head_watch, moved=None):
    """Calls of each changed function present on both sides, paired by test and call index (record.pair). A pair whose
    outputs differ on equal inputs is kept only if a second run of its test, on each side, gives the same two outputs:
    a difference neither side repeats is nondeterminism, counted and not shown."""
    rows, counts = record.pair([c for c in calls_b if c['function'] in both], [c for c in calls_a if c['function'] in both], moved)
    tests = sorted({row['test'] for row in rows})  # one representative test per distinct row
    kept, unstable = rows, 0
    if tests:
        again = {}
        for side, watch, targets in (('before', base_watch, plan['targets_before']), ('after', head_watch, plan['targets_after'])):
            folder = Path(scratch)/f'record-{side}-again'
            env = record.prepare(folder, trees[side], watch, targets)
            _chunks(execute, runner, python, trees[side], tests, scratch, f'{side}-again', RERUN, deadline, parts, env, chunk)
            again[side] = {(c['test'], c['function'], c['n']): c.get('result') or c['output'] for c in record.read(folder, trees[side],
                                                                                                runner.cwd(trees[side]))[1]}
        kept = [row for row in rows if again['before'].get((row['test'], row['function'], row['n'])) == row['digest'][0]
                and again['after'].get((row['test'], row['function'], row['n'])) == row['digest'][1]]
        unstable = len(rows) - len(kept)
    called = sorted({c['function'] for c in calls_b if c['function'] in both} | {c['function'] for c in calls_a if c['function'] in both})
    return dict(rows=kept, counts=dict(counts, unstable=unstable), called=called, compared_functions=len(both))


def plan_hunks(edits, before_src, after_src):
    """Every hunk of the changed production files (tests are the change's own tests, replayed apart)."""
    return [h for path, edit in edits.items() if path.endswith('.py') and not replay.is_test_file(path)
            for h in hunk_split.split(path, edit, before_src.get(path) or '', after_src.get(path) or '')]


def run(execute, runner, python, trees, edits, before_src, after_src, plan, scratch, budget, deadline, parts, chunk,
        remembered, cache_folder):
    """Both sides of the change, chosen and run as the module says. Returns a dict: ids (the candidates run on the code
    after the change, in order), before/after ({id: state}), context, sources ({id: where it came from}), mode, hunks
    (each with the tests that ran it on each side), recorded coverage and calls per side, seconds, problems."""
    hunks = plan_hunks(edits, before_src, after_src)
    base_watch, head_watch = {}, {}
    for h in hunks:
        base_watch.setdefault(h['path'], set()).update(h['base'])
        head_watch.setdefault(h['path'], set()).update(h['head'])
    # Every function a hunk changes, on each side where it exists, is recorded in that side's own run (record).
    moved = {}
    for h in hunks:
        for qual in set(h['old_touched']) & set(h['new_touched']):
            found = hunk_split.changed_defaults(before_src.get(h['path']) or '', after_src.get(h['path']) or '', qual)
            if found:
                moved[f"{h['path']}#{qual}"] = found
    targets_before = sorted({(h['path'], qual, tuple(sorted(moved.get(f"{h['path']}#{qual}", {}))))
                             for h in hunks for qual in h['old_touched']})
    targets_after = sorted({(h['path'], qual, tuple(sorted(moved.get(f"{h['path']}#{qual}", {}))))
                            for h in hunks for qual in h['new_touched']})
    plan = dict(plan, targets_before=targets_before, targets_after=targets_after)
    own = list(dict.fromkeys(plan.get('own') or []))
    mine = set(own)
    static = [i for i in plan.get('static') or [] if i not in mine]
    everything = [i for i in plan.get('everything') or [] if i not in mine]
    durations = remembered.get('durations') or {}
    kept = Coverage(cache_folder, plan.get('key'))
    suite = remembered.get('suite_seconds')
    fits = suite is None or suite <= budget * FILL
    # What a kept recording of this commit already says about each hunk; None where it cannot speak.
    known = {(h['path'], h['index']): kept.tests(h['path'], before_src.get(h['path']), h['base']) if h['base'] else None
             for h in hunks}
    # A recording runs unless the suite is known not to fit and this commit's kept recording speaks for every hunk with
    # code before the change.
    exploring = fits or any(h['base'] and known[h['path'], h['index']] is None for h in hunks)
    if exploring:
        # Static candidates first, so a run the budget stops still has their outcomes; then the rest, quickest first.
        first = set(static)
        rest = sorted((i for i in everything if i not in first), key=lambda i: (durations.get(i, 0.5), i))
        base_ids = list(dict.fromkeys([*static, *rest]))
    else:
        base_ids = None  # chosen from the kept recording below, then run
    sources, gaps = {}, []
    before_dir = Path(scratch)/'record-before'
    env = record.prepare(before_dir, trees['before'], base_watch, plan.get('targets_before') or [])
    coverage_b, calls_b = {}, []
    if base_ids is not None:
        found_b, problems_b, seconds_b, _ = _chunks(execute, runner, python, trees['before'], base_ids, scratch, 'before',
                                                   budget, deadline, parts, env, WHOLE if fits else chunk)
        coverage_b, calls_b, skipped_b = record.read(before_dir, trees['before'], runner.cwd(trees['before']))
        complete = bool(base_ids) and all(i in found_b for i in base_ids) and any(
            state in ('passed', 'failed', 'skipped') for state in found_b.values())
    else:
        found_b, problems_b, seconds_b, complete, skipped_b = {}, [], 0.0, False, {}
    mode = ALL if exploring and complete and seconds_b <= budget * FILL else COVERAGE
    if exploring and complete:
        remembered['suite_seconds'] = seconds_b
        kept.store(before_src, {p: v for p, v in base_watch.items() if v}, coverage_b, len(base_ids))
    elif exploring and not complete and fits:
        # The whole suite did not fit: next time the kept recording, or the static graph, chooses.
        remembered['suite_seconds'] = max(seconds_b, budget)
    for h in hunks:
        key = (h['path'], h['index'])
        if complete or not exploring:
            ran = record.tests_on(coverage_b, h['path'], h['base']) if exploring else known.get(key)
        else:
            ran = None
        h['base_tests'] = sorted(t for t in (ran or ()) if t != record.IMPORT) if ran is not None else None
        h['at_import'] = bool(ran and record.IMPORT in ran)
    if mode == ALL:
        head_ids = [*own, *base_ids]
        sources.update({i: ALL for i in base_ids})
    else:
        chosen = []
        for h in hunks:
            if h['base_tests'] is not None and not (h['at_import'] and not h['base_tests']):
                chosen += [t for t in h['base_tests'] if t not in mine]
                sources.update({t: COVERAGE for t in h['base_tests'] if t not in mine and t not in sources})
        if any(h['base_tests'] is None or (h['at_import'] and not h['base_tests']) for h in hunks) or not hunks:
            chosen += static
            for t in static:
                sources.setdefault(t, STATIC)
        head_ids = list(dict.fromkeys([*own, *chosen]))
    sources.update({i: OWN for i in own})
    after_dir = Path(scratch)/'record-after'
    env = record.prepare(after_dir, trees['after'], head_watch, plan.get('targets_after') or [])
    found_a, problems_a, seconds_a, context = _chunks(execute, runner, python, trees['after'], head_ids, scratch, 'after',
                                                      budget, deadline, parts, env, WHOLE if mode == ALL else chunk)
    coverage_a, calls_a, skipped_a = record.read(after_dir, trees['after'], runner.cwd(trees['after']))
    # Candidates the code before the change has not run yet (chosen from a kept recording, or from the static graph):
    # run there too, so each outcome on the changed code has its partner.
    missing = [i for i in head_ids if i not in mine and i in found_a and i not in found_b]
    if missing:
        env = record.prepare(Path(scratch)/'record-before-2', trees['before'], base_watch, plan.get('targets_before') or [])
        more, said, took, _ = _chunks(execute, runner, python, trees['before'], missing, scratch, 'before-2',
                                      max(budget - seconds_b, budget * (1 - FILL)), deadline, parts, env, chunk)
        found_b.update(more)
        problems_b += [p for p in said if p not in problems_b]
        seconds_b += took
        cov2, calls2, _ = record.read(Path(scratch)/'record-before-2', trees['before'], runner.cwd(trees['before']))
        for test, files in cov2.items():
            for path, lines in files.items():
                coverage_b.setdefault(test, {}).setdefault(path, set()).update(lines)
        calls_b += calls2
    for h in hunks:
        h['head_tests'] = sorted(t for t in record.tests_on(coverage_a, h['path'], h['head']) if t != record.IMPORT)
        h['head_at_import'] = record.IMPORT in record.tests_on(coverage_a, h['path'], h['head'])
    paired = compare(execute, runner, python, trees, plan, scratch, deadline, parts, chunk, calls_b, calls_a,
                     {f'{t[0]}#{t[1]}' for t in targets_before} & {f'{t[0]}#{t[1]}' for t in targets_after}, base_watch,
                     head_watch, moved)
    cut = []
    if 'wall cap' in problems_a or ('wall cap' in problems_b and not found_a):
        cut.append(f'{sum(i not in found_a for i in head_ids)} of {len(head_ids)} candidate tests')
    if 'wall cap' in problems_b and base_ids is not None and not complete:
        cut.append(f'the code before the change: {sum(i not in found_b for i in base_ids)} of {len(base_ids)} tests')
    problems_a = [p for p in problems_a if p != 'wall cap']
    problems_b = [p for p in problems_b if p != 'wall cap']
    if exploring and not complete and not cut:
        gaps.append(f"the code before the change ran {len(found_b)} of {len(base_ids)} tests in its {budget} s: not the "
                    f"whole suite, so the static graph adds candidates for every hunk")
    return dict(ids=head_ids, before=found_b, after=found_a, context=context, sources=sources, mode=mode, hunks=hunks,
                coverage=dict(before=coverage_b, after=coverage_a), calls=dict(before=calls_b, after=calls_a),
                skipped={**skipped_b, **skipped_a}, seconds=dict(before=seconds_b, after=seconds_a),
                problems=dict(before=problems_b, after=problems_a), base_complete=complete,
                base_planned=len(base_ids) if base_ids is not None else 0, gaps=gaps, cut=cut, paired=paired,
                targets=dict(before=targets_before, after=targets_after))

230	                _local.busy = False
231	            # The arguments as the call leaves them, without those held apart (their value is the default itself).
232	            stack.append((code, dict(k="call", t=_state["test"], fn=target, n=n, i=digest, ishow=shown, args=kept,
233	                                     **({"dp": held} if held else {}))))
234	            return None

236	        def _end(code, result):
237	            stack = getattr(_local, "stack", None)
238	            while stack:
239	                top, record = stack.pop()
240	                if top is code:
241	                    break
242	            else:
243	                return
244	            if record is None:
245	                return
246	            _local.busy = True
247	            try:
248	                after = _fp(record.pop("args")) if record.get("args") is not None else None
249	                out, shown = _pack([result, after])
250	                result_digest, result_shown = _pack(result)
251	                record.update(o=out, oshow=result_shown, r=result_digest, ashow=_pack(after)[1])

383	def identity(raw, tree, cwd=None):
384	    """AMU's id (path::Class::test) for a recorded test name: a pytest node id without its parameters, or a dotted
385	    unittest id resolved to its file under ``cwd`` (the runner's directory) or ``tree``."""
386	    if raw == IMPORT or not raw:
387	        return IMPORT
388	    if '::' in raw:
389	        path, *rest = raw.split('::')
390	        return '::'.join([path, *rest[:-1], PARAMS.sub('', rest[-1])]) if rest else path
391	    parts = raw.split(' ')[0].split('.')
392	    for base in [b for b in (cwd, tree) if b is not None]:
393	        for cut in range(len(parts) - 1, 0, -1):
394	            file = Path(base)/('/'.join(parts[:cut]) + '.py')
395	            if file.is_file():

397	                    path = file.resolve().relative_to(Path(tree).resolve()).as_posix()
398	                except ValueError:

405	    """What a run recorded: ({test: {path: {line}}}, [call], {function: why not recorded})."""

417	                continue  # a line cut short when the run was stopped
418	            raw = event.get('t', IMPORT)

421	                test = names[raw] = identity(raw, tree, cwd)

425	                for path, found in event.get('f', {}).items():

427	            elif kind == 'call':

429	                                  output=event.get('o'), input_shown=event.get('ishow', ''), output_shown=event.get('oshow', ''),
430	                                  result=event.get('r'), after_shown=event.get('ashow', ''), held=event.get('dp') or {}))

447	def pair(before, after, defaults=None):
448	    """Calls recorded on each side, paired by (test, function, call index). Returns (rows, counts): a row for each pair
449	    whose inputs are equal and whose outputs differ. A call with no partner, or whose inputs differ, is counted, never
450	    compared.
451	
452	    ``defaults``: {function: {parameter: (its default before, after)}} for parameters whose default the change alters
453	    (``literal`` forms, None when not a plain value). Such a parameter is outside the input digest; the inputs count as
454	    equal when it holds the same value on both sides, or when each side holds its own default (the caller left it out),
455	    and the row says which parameters it assumed so."""
456	    left = {(c['test'], c['function'], c['n']): c for c in before if c['test'] != IMPORT}
457	    right = {(c['test'], c['function'], c['n']): c for c in after if c['test'] != IMPORT}
458	    rows, counts = [], dict(paired=0, compared=0, inputs_differ=0, unpaired=0, unreadable=0)
459	    for key in sorted(set(left) | set(right)):
460	        old, new = left.get(key), right.get(key)
461	        if old is None or new is None:
462	            counts['unpaired'] += 1
463	            continue
464	        counts['paired'] += 1
465	        if not old['input'] or not new['input'] or old['output'] is None or new['output'] is None:
466	            counts['unreadable'] += 1
467	            continue
468	        if old['input'] != new['input']:
469	            counts['inputs_differ'] += 1
470	            continue
471	        assumed = []
472	        changed = (defaults or {}).get(key[1], {})
473	        for name in set(old.get('held') or {}) | set(new.get('held') or {}):
474	            was, now = (old.get('held') or {}).get(name), (new.get('held') or {}).get(name)
475	            if was == now:
476	                continue
477	            given = changed.get(name, (None, None))
478	            if given[0] is not None and was == given[0] and now == given[1]:
479	                assumed.append(name)
480	                continue
481	            assumed = None
482	            break
483	        if assumed is None:
484	            counts['inputs_differ'] += 1
485	            continue
486	        counts['compared'] += 1
487	        # The output compared is the return value or the exception. The arguments as the call left them are shown, not
488	        # compared: what a call leaves on its arguments is mostly lazy caches filled earlier or later on one side.
489	        if (old.get('result') or old['output']) != (new.get('result') or new['output']):
490	            differs = ['result']
491	            rows.append(dict(test=key[0], function=key[1], n=key[2], input=old['input_shown'] + (
492	                             f" [{', '.join(sorted(assumed))} left at each side's default]" if assumed else ''), differs=differs,
493	                             before=old['output_shown'], after=new['output_shown'],
494	                             before_args=old.get('after_shown', ''), after_args=new.get('after_shown', ''),
495	                             digest=(old.get('result') or old['output'], new.get('result') or new['output'])))
496	    # The same difference on the same input, seen in several tests or calls, is one row with its count.
497	    unique = {}
498	    for row in rows:
499	        key = (row['function'], row['input'], row['digest'])
500	        if key in unique:
501	            unique[key]['seen'] += 1
502	        else:
503	            unique[key] = dict(row, seen=1)
504	    counts['differing_calls'] = len(rows)
505	    return list(unique.values()), counts

1	"""Execution-first selection: which tests run on each side of a change, chosen from what the tests were seen to run.
2	
3	The order of evidence:
4	
5	1. **The whole suite.** When the suite's last measured time on the code before the change fits the budget, or no
6	   time was measured yet, every test runs on that side, recorded (record module). If that run finishes inside the
7	   planned share of the budget, every test also runs on the code after the change: no selection.
8	2. **Coverage of the changed code.** Otherwise the candidates are the tests the recording saw entering the code each
9	   hunk changes (hunks module): this run's recording, or one kept for the same commit (``Coverage``).
10	3. **The static graph**, only for a hunk no recording can speak for: code the change adds where nothing ran before, a
11	   hunk whose file was not recorded, a module-level hunk that runs at import, or a recording that did not finish.
12	
13	Every candidate keeps where it came from (``sources``), and each hunk the tests that ran it on each side.
14	"""
15	from __future__ import annotations

27	ALL, COVERAGE, STATIC, OWN = 'all of the suite', 'coverage', 'static graph', "the change's own test"

30	def _sha(text):
31	    return hashlib.sha256((text or '').encode()).hexdigest()[:16]

34	class Coverage:
35	    """Per-test coverage of changed files on one commit, kept between runs (the CI cache is keyed by the merge base).
36	    For each file: the hash of its text, the lines that were watched, and {line: [test]}. Only a recording of the whole
37	    suite is kept, so a watched line nobody ran was run by no test."""
38	
39	    def __init__(self, folder, key):
40	        self.path = Path(folder)/'coverage'/f'{key}.json' if folder and key else None
41	        try:
42	            self.data = json.loads(self.path.read_text()) if self.path else {}
43	        except (OSError, ValueError):
44	            self.data = {}
45	
46	    def tests(self, path, text, lines):
47	        """Tests that ran any of ``lines``, or None when this commit's recording did not watch all of them."""
48	        entry = (self.data.get('files') or {}).get(path)
49	        if not entry or entry.get('sha') != _sha(text) or not set(lines) <= set(entry.get('watched', [])):
50	            return None
51	        hits = entry.get('hits', {})
52	        return {test for line in lines for test in hits.get(str(line), [])}
53	
54	    def store(self, before_src, watched, coverage, tests_run):
55	        if not self.path:
56	            return
57	        files = dict(self.data.get('files') or {})
58	        for path, lines in watched.items():
59	            hits = {}
60	            for test, seen in coverage.items():
61	                for line in seen.get(path, ()):
62	                    hits.setdefault(str(line), []).append(test)
63	            files[path] = dict(sha=_sha(before_src.get(path)), watched=sorted(lines), hits={k: sorted(v) for k, v in hits.items()})
64	        try:
65	            self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
66	            self.path.write_text(json.dumps(dict(files=files, tests=tests_run)))
67	        except OSError:
68	            pass

71	def _chunks(execute, runner, python, tree, ids, scratch, name, budget, deadline, parts, env, chunk):
72	    """Run ``ids`` in order, a chunk at a time, until they are done or ``budget`` seconds are used. Returns
73	    ({id: state}, [problems], seconds, {id: the slice it ran in}); ``problems`` holds 'wall cap' when the deadline
74	    stopped it."""
75	    found, problems, context, began = {}, [], {}, time.perf_counter()
76	    for start in range(0, len(ids), chunk * parts):
77	        left = budget - (time.perf_counter() - began)
78	        if deadline is not None:
79	            if deadline - time.monotonic() <= 1:
80	                problems.append('wall cap')
81	                break
82	            left = min(left, deadline - time.monotonic())
83	        if left <= 1:
84	            break
85	        part = ids[start:start + chunk * parts]
86	        got, said = execute(runner, python, tree, part, scratch, f'{name}-{start}', left, parts, env)
87	        found.update(got)
88	        for slice_ in [part[i::parts] for i in range(parts)] if parts > 1 else [part]:
89	            context.update({ident: slice_ for ident in slice_})
90	        problems += [p for p in said if p not in problems]
91	        if 'timed out' in said:
92	            if deadline is not None and deadline - time.monotonic() <= 1:
93	                problems.append('wall cap')
94	            break
95	    return found, problems, round(time.perf_counter() - began, 1), context

101	def compare(execute, runner, python, trees, plan, scratch, deadline, parts, chunk, calls_b, calls_a, both, base_watch,
102	            head_watch, moved=None):
103	    """Calls of each changed function present on both sides, paired by test and call index (record.pair). A pair whose
104	    outputs differ on equal inputs is kept only if a second run of its test, on each side, gives the same two outputs:
105	    a difference neither side repeats is nondeterminism, counted and not shown."""
106	    rows, counts = record.pair([c for c in calls_b if c['function'] in both], [c for c in calls_a if c['function'] in both], moved)
107	    tests = sorted({row['test'] for row in rows})  # one representative test per distinct row
108	    kept, unstable = rows, 0
109	    if tests:
110	        again = {}
111	        for side, watch, targets in (('before', base_watch, plan['targets_before']), ('after', head_watch, plan['targets_after'])):
112	            folder = Path(scratch)/f'record-{side}-again'
113	            env = record.prepare(folder, trees[side], watch, targets)
114	            _chunks(execute, runner, python, trees[side], tests, scratch, f'{side}-again', RERUN, deadline, parts, env, chunk)
115	            again[side] = {(c['test'], c['function'], c['n']): c.get('result') or c['output'] for c in record.read(folder, trees[side],
116	                                                                                                runner.cwd(trees[side]))[1]}
117	        kept = [row for row in rows if again['before'].get((row['test'], row['function'], row['n'])) == row['digest'][0]
118	                and again['after'].get((row['test'], row['function'], row['n'])) == row['digest'][1]]
119	        unstable = len(rows) - len(kept)
120	    called = sorted({c['function'] for c in calls_b if c['function'] in both} | {c['function'] for c in calls_a if c['function'] in both})
121	    return dict(rows=kept, counts=dict(counts, unstable=unstable), called=called, compared_functions=len(both))

124	def plan_hunks(edits, before_src, after_src):
125	    """Every hunk of the changed production files (tests are the change's own tests, replayed apart)."""
126	    return [h for path, edit in edits.items() if path.endswith('.py') and not replay.is_test_file(path)
127	            for h in hunk_split.split(path, edit, before_src.get(path) or '', after_src.get(path) or '')]

130	def run(execute, runner, python, trees, edits, before_src, after_src, plan, scratch, budget, deadline, parts, chunk,
131	        remembered, cache_folder):
132	    """Both sides of the change, chosen and run as the module says. Returns a dict: ids (the candidates run on the code
133	    after the change, in order), before/after ({id: state}), context, sources ({id: where it came from}), mode, hunks
134	    (each with the tests that ran it on each side), recorded coverage and calls per side, seconds, problems."""
135	    hunks = plan_hunks(edits, before_src, after_src)
136	    base_watch, head_watch = {}, {}
137	    for h in hunks:
138	        base_watch.setdefault(h['path'], set()).update(h['base'])
139	        head_watch.setdefault(h['path'], set()).update(h['head'])
140	    # Every function a hunk changes, on each side where it exists, is recorded in that side's own run (record).
141	    moved = {}
142	    for h in hunks:
143	        for qual in set(h['old_touched']) & set(h['new_touched']):
144	            found = hunk_split.changed_defaults(before_src.get(h['path']) or '', after_src.get(h['path']) or '', qual)
145	            if found:
146	                moved[f"{h['path']}#{qual}"] = found
147	    targets_before = sorted({(h['path'], qual, tuple(sorted(moved.get(f"{h['path']}#{qual}", {}))))
148	                             for h in hunks for qual in h['old_touched']})
149	    targets_after = sorted({(h['path'], qual, tuple(sorted(moved.get(f"{h['path']}#{qual}", {}))))
150	                            for h in hunks for qual in h['new_touched']})
151	    plan = dict(plan, targets_before=targets_before, targets_after=targets_after)
152	    own = list(dict.fromkeys(plan.get('own') or []))
153	    mine = set(own)
154	    static = [i for i in plan.get('static') or [] if i not in mine]
155	    everything = [i for i in plan.get('everything') or [] if i not in mine]
156	    durations = remembered.get('durations') or {}

159	    fits = suite is None or suite <= budget * FILL
160	    # What a kept recording of this commit already says about each hunk; None where it cannot speak.
161	    known = {(h['path'], h['index']): kept.tests(h['path'], before_src.get(h['path']), h['base']) if h['base'] else None
162	             for h in hunks}

164	    # code before the change.
165	    exploring = fits or any(h['base'] and known[h['path'], h['index']] is None for h in hunks)
166	    if exploring:
167	        # Static candidates first, so a run the budget stops still has their outcomes; then the rest, quickest first.
168	        first = set(static)
169	        rest = sorted((i for i in everything if i not in first), key=lambda i: (durations.get(i, 0.5), i))
170	        base_ids = list(dict.fromkeys([*static, *rest]))

172	        base_ids = None  # chosen from the kept recording below, then run
173	    sources, gaps = {}, []

1	"""Execution records from a side's own test run (Python 3.12 and later): which watched lines each test ran, and each
2	call into a watched function with a digest of what went in and what came out.
3	
4	The hook is a ``sitecustomize`` on ``AMU_TRUST_PATH``, so every interpreter the run starts loads it, whatever the runner.
5	It uses one ``sys.monitoring`` tool id:
6	
7	- ``PY_START`` on every code object once. A code object outside the watched files is switched off for the run (DISABLE).
8	  One in a watched file gets local ``LINE`` events when it holds a watched line, and local ``PY_RETURN`` when it is a
9	  watched function; ``PY_START`` stays on only for watched functions.
10	- ``LINE`` records (test, file, line) and returns DISABLE; at every test boundary ``restart_events()`` switches the lines
11	  back on, so each watched line costs one event per test.
12	- ``PY_UNWIND`` (global: it cannot be set per code object) closes a watched call that ended in an exception.
13	
14	A call's input is fingerprinted when it starts, from its arguments' structure and state (``__dict__`` and ``__slots__``
15	read with ``object.__getattribute__``, never ``repr`` or ``__eq__`` of a project object); its output is the fingerprint of
16	the return value or the exception, and of the arguments when it ended. Both sides are recorded the same way, in their
17	own runs, on objects their own code built: two calls are compared only when their inputs' fingerprints are equal.
18	
19	The test a record belongs to is the pytest node id (a plugin named in ``PYTEST_PLUGINS``) or the unittest id
20	(``TestCase.run`` wrapped); code that runs outside any test, such as a module body at collection, is ``<import>``.
21	"""
22	from __future__ import annotations
23	
24	import json
25	import re
26	from pathlib import Path
27	
28	IMPORT = '<import>'
29	CALLS = 20          # calls recorded per (test, function)
30	PER_FUNCTION = 4000  # calls recorded per function per process
31	PREVIEW = 300        # characters kept of an input or output shown in a report
32	
33	HOOK = r'''
34	import os as _os, sys as _sys
35	_spec_path = _os.environ.get("AMU_REC_SPEC")
36	if _spec_path and _sys.version_info >= (3, 12):
37	    try:
38	        import atexit, hashlib, json, re, threading, types
39	        with open(_spec_path) as _h:
40	            _spec = json.load(_h)

42	        _prefixes = sorted({_root, _os.path.abspath(_spec["root"])}, key=len, reverse=True)
43	        _m = _sys.monitoring
44	        _tool = next(i for i in (5, 4, 3) if _m.get_tool(i) is None)
45	        _m.use_tool_id(_tool, "amu-record")
46	        _E = _m.events
47	        _lines = {_os.path.realpath(_os.path.join(_root, f)): set(v) for f, v in _spec["lines"].items()}
48	        _targets = {(_os.path.realpath(_os.path.join(_root, t[0])), t[1]): t[0] + "#" + t[1] for t in _spec["targets"]}
49	        # Parameters whose default the change alters: left out of the input digest, kept apart (pair decides).
50	        _apart = {t[0] + "#" + t[1]: set(t[2]) for t in _spec["targets"] if len(t) > 2 and t[2]}
51	        _files = set(_lines) | {k[0] for k in _targets}
52	        _rel = {p: _os.path.relpath(p, _root) for p in _files}
53	        _limit, _per = _spec.get("calls", 20), _spec.get("per_function", 4000)
54	        _keep = _spec.get("preview", 300)
55	        _out = _os.path.join(_spec["out"], "%d.jsonl" % _os.getpid())
56	        _state = {"test": _os.environ.get("AMU_TEST_CONTEXT") or "<import>", "pytest": False}
57	        _codes = {}
58	        _hits = {}
59	        _counts = {}
60	        _totals = {}
61	        _buffer = []
62	        _local = threading.local()
63	        _ADDRESS = re.compile(r" at 0x[0-9a-fA-F]+")
64	        _GEN = 0x20 | 0x80 | 0x100 | 0x200
65	
66	        def _flush():
67	            if _hits:
68	                _buffer.append(json.dumps(dict(k="cov", t=_state["test"], f={_rel[p]: sorted(v) for p, v in _hits.items()})))
69	                _hits.clear()
70	            if _buffer:
71	                try:
72	                    with open(_out, "a") as handle:
73	                        handle.write("\n".join(_buffer) + "\n")
74	                except Exception:
75	                    pass
76	                del _buffer[:]
77	
78	        def _begin(test):
79	            _flush()
80	            _state["test"] = test
81	            _counts.clear()
82	            _m.restart_events()
83	
84	        def _fp(value, depth=0, seen=()):
85	            kind = type(value)
86	            if value is None or kind in (bool, int, float, complex):
87	                return repr(value)
88	            if kind is str:
89	                # Each side runs in its own copy of the tree: where that copy is, is not what the code did.
90	                for prefix in _prefixes:
91	                    if prefix in value:
92	                        value = value.replace(prefix, "<root>")
93	                return repr(value) if len(value) <= 2000 else repr(value[:2000]) + "+%d" % len(value)
94	            if kind is bytes:
95	                return repr(value) if len(value) <= 2000 else repr(value[:2000]) + "+%d" % len(value)
96	            if depth > 4 or id(value) in seen:
97	                return "<" + kind.__qualname__ + ">"
98	            seen = (*seen, id(value))
99	            if kind in (list, tuple):
100	                items = [_fp(v, depth + 1, seen) for v in value[:100]]
101	                return [kind.__name__, items, len(value)]
102	            if kind in (set, frozenset):
103	                items = sorted((_fp(v, depth + 1, seen) for v in list(value)[:100]), key=repr)
104	                return [kind.__name__, items, len(value)]
105	            if kind is dict:
106	                named = value.get("__name__") if "__builtins__" in value else None
107	                module = _sys.modules.get(named) if type(named) is str else None
108	                if module is not None and getattr(module, "__dict__", None) is value:
109	                    return "globals:" + named  # a module's namespace: its name, not everything defined in it
110	                pairs = [[_fp(k, depth + 1, seen), _fp(v, depth + 1, seen)] for k, v in list(value.items())[:100]]
111	                return ["dict", pairs, len(value)]
112	            if isinstance(value, type):
113	                return "type:" + getattr(value, "__module__", "?") + "." + getattr(value, "__qualname__", "?")
114	            if isinstance(value, (types.FunctionType, types.BuiltinFunctionType, types.MethodType)):
115	                return "fn:" + str(getattr(value, "__module__", "?")) + "." + str(getattr(value, "__qualname__", "?"))
116	            if isinstance(value, types.ModuleType):
117	                return "module:" + value.__name__
118	            name = getattr(kind, "__module__", "?") + "." + kind.__qualname__
119	            state = None
120	            try:
121	                found = object.__getattribute__(value, "__dict__")
122	                if type(found) is dict:
123	                    # A value cached under a name the class defines as a non-data descriptor (a cached property) is
124	                    # derived state: whether it was computed yet says when it was asked for, not what the object is.
125	                    state = {k: v for k, v in found.items() if not _cached(kind, k)}
126	            except Exception:
127	                pass
128	            slots = []
129	            for klass in kind.__mro__:
130	                names = klass.__dict__.get("__slots__", ())
131	                for slot in ((names,) if isinstance(names, str) else names):
132	                    if slot in ("__dict__", "__weakref__"):
133	                        continue
134	                    try:
135	                        slots.append([slot, _fp(object.__getattribute__(value, slot), depth + 1, seen)])
136	                    except AttributeError:
137	                        slots.append([slot, "<unset>"])
138	                    except Exception as exc:
139	                        slots.append([slot, "<" + type(exc).__name__ + ">"])
140	            if state is not None or slots:
141	                return [name, _fp(state, depth + 1, seen) if state is not None else None, slots]
142	            try:
143	                text = repr(value)
144	            except Exception as exc:
145	                text = "<repr failed: " + type(exc).__name__ + ">"
146	            return name + ":" + _ADDRESS.sub(" at 0x?", text)[:2000]
147	
148	        def _cached(kind, name):
149	            for klass in kind.__mro__:
150	                attribute = klass.__dict__.get(name)
151	                if attribute is not None:
152	                    # Any descriptor serving that name (a cached property, with or without __set__): the instance
153	                    # dict entry is its cache. Plain methods are not descriptors of state.
154	                    return (hasattr(type(attribute), "__get__")
155	                            and not isinstance(attribute, (types.FunctionType, staticmethod, classmethod)))
156	            return False
157	
158	        def _pack(value):
159	            text = json.dumps(value, default=str)
160	            return hashlib.sha1(text.encode()).hexdigest()[:16], text[:_keep]
161	
162	        def _names(code):
163	            count = code.co_argcount + code.co_kwonlyargcount
164	            names = list(code.co_varnames[:count])
165	            if code.co_flags & 0x04:
166	                names.append(code.co_varnames[count])
167	                count += 1
168	            if code.co_flags & 0x08:
169	                names.append(code.co_varnames[count])
170	            return names
171	
172	        def _arguments(code, frame):
173	            count = code.co_argcount + code.co_kwonlyargcount
174	            names = list(code.co_varnames[:count])
175	            if code.co_flags & 0x04:
176	                names.append(code.co_varnames[count])
177	                count += 1
178	            if code.co_flags & 0x08:
179	                names.append(code.co_varnames[count])
180	            return [frame.f_locals.get(n) for n in names]
181	
182	        def _start(code, offset):
183	            known = _codes.get(code)
184	            if known is None:
185	                name = code.co_filename
186	                path = _os.path.realpath(name) if name and not name.startswith("<") else ""
187	                if path not in _files:
188	                    known = False
189	                else:
190	                    own = {line for _, _, line in code.co_lines() if line} & _lines.get(path, set())
191	                    target = _targets.get((path, code.co_qualname))
192	                    if target and code.co_flags & _GEN:
193	                        _buffer.append(json.dumps(dict(k="skip", fn=target, why="generator or coroutine")))
194	                        target = None
195	                    events = (_E.LINE if own else 0) | (_E.PY_RETURN if target else 0)
196	                    if events:
197	                        _m.set_local_events(_tool, code, events)
198	                    known = (path, target) if (own or target) else False
199	                _codes[code] = known
200	            if not known or not known[1]:
201	                return _m.DISABLE
202	            target = known[1]
203	            if getattr(_local, "busy", False):
204	                return None  # a project function the fingerprint itself reached: neither recorded nor closed
205	            key = (_state["test"], target)
206	            n = _counts.get(key, 0)
207	            _counts[key] = n + 1
208	            stack = getattr(_local, "stack", None)
209	            if stack is None:
210	                stack = _local.stack = []
211	            if n >= _limit or _totals.get(target, 0) >= _per:
212	                stack.append((code, None))
213	                return None
214	            _totals[target] = _totals.get(target, 0) + 1
215	            _local.busy = True
216	            try:
217	                frame = _sys._getframe(1)
218	                args = _arguments(code, frame)
219	                apart = _apart.get(target)
220	                if apart:
221	                    names = _names(code)
222	                    kept = [v for name, v in zip(names, args) if name not in apart]
223	                    held = {name: json.dumps(_fp(v), default=str) for name, v in zip(names, args) if name in apart}
224	                else:
225	                    kept, held = args, None
226	                digest, shown = _pack(_fp(kept))
227	            except Exception as exc:
228	                args, kept, held, digest, shown = None, None, None, None, "<" + type(exc).__name__ + ">"
229	            finally:
230	                _local.busy = False

232	            stack.append((code, dict(k="call", t=_state["test"], fn=target, n=n, i=digest, ishow=shown, args=kept,
233	                                     **({"dp": held} if held else {}))))
